issueContext.title: Use of outdated OpenTelemetry Go package
issueContext.body:
### What happened? Importing Kubernetes' `k8s.io/apiserver` module together with the latest version of `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` results in a failed build due to breaking changes in the OpenTelemetry Go library. This also happens with `k8s.io/component-base`. The solution is to bump the opentelemetry dependencies to a stable version. ### What did you expect to happen? `k8s.io/apiserver` should be usable in a module that uses a stable version of `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? A simple way to reproduce it is to create a new Go module via `go mod init example.com/kube-issue` that depends on the latest version of both `k8s.io/apiserver` and some new `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` module, e.g. `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc`.
main.go contents ```go package main import ( _ "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc" _ "k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters" ) ```
If you try to do `go mod tidy` you can see a bunch of errors (which come from breaking changes on the OpenTelemetry Go libraries).
go mod tidy output ``` ❯ go mod tidy go: finding module for package go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc go: downloading go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace v1.2.0 go: downloading go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc v1.2.0 go: found go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc v1.2.0 go: downloading go.opentelemetry.io/proto/otlp v0.10.0 go: finding module for package go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv go: finding module for package go.opentelemetry.io/otel/unit go: finding module for package go.opentelemetry.io/otel/internal/metric go: found go.opentelemetry.io/otel/internal/me

enrichment.problem: The API server's OpenTelemetry root span was named "KubernetesAPI", which deviated from standard HTTP naming conventions and could cause confusion or mismatched expectations in tracing backends.
enrichment.affected: Users instrumenting the kube-apiserver with OpenTelemetry; any downstream tracing systems that rely on the root span name for filtering or analysis.
enrichment.fix: The root span name is updated to "HTTP GET", aligning it with typical HTTP request tracing semantics.
enrichment.impact: Observability tools and dashboards that consume OpenTelemetry traces will see a clearer, more consistent span name, simplifying query patterns and improving trace readability for API server traffic.

feature.description: Added `--disable-compression` flag to `kubectl` (default = false). When true, it opts out of response compression for all requests to the `apiserver`. This can help improve list call latencies significantly when client-server network bandwidth is ample (>30MB/s) or if the server is CPU-constrained.
feature.author: shyamjvs
feature.userFacingChange: A new --disable-compression flag has been added to kubectl (default = false). When true, it opts out of response compression for all requests to the apiserver. This can help improve list call latencies significantly when client-server network bandwidth is ample (>30MB/s) or if the server is CPU-constrained.

enrichment.problem: kubectl always requested compressed responses from the apiserver, which can add CPU overhead and increase latency for list operations when network bandwidth is plentiful or the apiserver is CPU‑constrained.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users performing list/watch calls, especially in clusters with high client‑server bandwidth (>30 MB/s) or apiserver CPU pressure.
enrichment.fix: Adds a new `--disable-compression` flag (default false) that, when enabled, tells kubectl to opt out of response compression for all apiserver requests.
enrichment.impact: Users can reduce apiserver CPU usage and achieve noticeably lower list call latencies in high‑bandwidth or CPU‑starved environments.

feature.description: kubeadm: now supports image repository format validation.
feature.author: SataQiu
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: support image repository format validation

enrichment.problem: kubeadm did not validate the format of container image repositories during init/join, allowing invalid repository strings that could cause image pull failures later.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using kubeadm to bootstrap a cluster with custom image repositories; clusters that would have encountered pull failures due to malformed repository URLs.
enrichment.fix: Added repository format validation to kubeadm, rejecting malformed image repository specifications early in the workflow.
enrichment.impact: Users get immediate feedback on invalid image repository definitions, preventing later pull errors and improving cluster bootstrap reliability.

feature.description: Exposed health check SLI metrics on `metrics/slis` for apiserver.
feature.author: logicalhan
feature.userFacingChange: Expose health check SLI metrics on "metrics/slis" for apiserver

enrichment.problem: Kube-apiserver did not expose health check Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics, so operators could not directly observe health check performance via the standard metrics endpoint.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the kube-apiserver; any monitoring system that scrapes apiserver metrics.
enrichment.fix: Adds a new metrics endpoint `metrics/slis` on the apiserver that emits health‑check SLI metrics, making them available to Prometheus and other observability stacks.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor apiserver health‑check latency and success rates, set alerts, and gain better insight into API availability, improving cluster reliability and troubleshooting.

feature.description: Added a new feature gate `CelValidatingAdmissionExtensibility` to enable expression validation for Admission Control.
feature.author: cici37

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes admission control lacked native support for validating resources using CEL (Common Expression Language) expressions, limiting extensibility and expressive validation capabilities.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where admission validation is needed and administrators want to use CEL expressions; enables existing and future admission plugins to leverage CEL validation.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new feature gate `CelValidatingAdmissionExtensibility` that, when enabled, activates CEL‑based expression validation for admission control, allowing admission plugins to use CEL for fine‑grained validation logic.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators and developers can now write concise, powerful validation rules using CEL without custom webhook code, improving security, reducing operational complexity, and enabling richer policy enforcement directly in the API server.

feature.description: The ExpandedDNSConfig feature has graduated to beta and is enabled by default. Note that this feature requires container runtime support.
feature.author: gjkim42

enrichment.problem: Before this change, the ExpandedDNSConfig feature was only alpha and required manual enabling, limiting users' ability to configure extended DNS options for pods.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that run containers with a runtime supporting the expanded DNS config; workloads that rely on custom DNS settings in pod specs.
enrichment.fix: The feature has graduated to beta and is now enabled by default in the cluster, automatically allowing pods to use the expanded DNS configuration when the underlying container runtime supports it.
enrichment.impact: Clusters gain richer DNS configuration capabilities without extra feature gates, simplifying pod spec authoring. Users must ensure their container runtime implements the required DNS support, otherwise pod DNS settings may be ignored or cause errors.

feature.description: The `LegacyServiceAccountTokenNoAutoGeneration` feature gate was promoted to GA.
feature.author: zshihang
feature.userFacingChange: The LegacyServiceAccountTokenNoAutoGeneration feature gate has been promoted to GA

enrichment.problem: Clusters without the LegacyServiceAccountTokenNoAutoGeneration feature gate enabled continued to auto‑generate long‑lived secret‑based service account tokens, which are less secure and increase secret sprawl.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that create ServiceAccounts; workloads that rely on automatically created legacy secret tokens will see those tokens no longer appear by default.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate has been promoted to GA and is now enabled by default. Legacy secret‑based service account tokens are no longer auto‑generated unless explicitly requested, aligning the default behavior with the security‑focused design of the project.
enrichment.impact: Improves cluster security by eliminating unnecessary secret tokens, reduces the surface for credential leakage, and encourages workloads to use projected service account tokens (BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume). Existing workloads that relied on auto‑generated legacy tokens must be updated to request a token explicitly.

feature.description: Added kubelet metrics to track the cpumanager cpu allocation and pinning
feature.author: fromanirh

issueContext.title: Add metrics for cpumanager
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add [metrics](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/v1.25.2/pkg/kubelet/metrics) to enable observability of the cpumanager.

### Why is this needed?

This is required to [GA the feature](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3350) but it's also useful in general.

To the best of my knowledge, it's very hard to observe the behavior of cpumanager without peeking into the pod and/or use the podresources interface (kubelet >= 1.24). But even for the latter, no well known components expose metrics consuming this information.

I believe anyway kubelet some expose some basic metrics about cpumanager behaviour, while deferring more fine grained metrics to external components (NFD, node_exporter, is fine)

enrichment.problem: There were no built‑in kubelet metrics exposing how the CPU manager allocated CPUs and performed pinning, making it difficult to observe, monitor, or troubleshoot CPU manager behavior.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes users who enable the CPU manager (static policy) and need visibility into CPU allocation/pinning, as well as monitoring systems that ingest kubelet metrics.
enrichment.fix: The change adds new kubelet metrics that report the number of CPUs allocated by the CPU manager and the pinning state of those CPUs. These metrics are exported via the existing kubelet metrics endpoint.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now monitor CPU manager activity through standard observability stacks, verify that the feature works as expected, and use the data to size workloads or diagnose placement issues. The metrics also satisfy a requirement for GA of the CPU manager feature.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.2
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes builds were using an older Go toolchain; the build process needed to be updated to a newer supported Go version.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and users building Kubernetes from source.
enrichment.fix: The build system and CI have been updated to compile Kubernetes with Go 1.19.2.
enrichment.impact: Provides access to Go 1.19 security patches, performance improvements, and ensures future compatibility; users building from source get the newer binaries without changes to runtime behavior.

feature.description:
'`registered_metric_total` will now report the number of metrics broken down by
stability level and deprecated version.'
feature.author: logicalhan
feature.userFacingChange: `registered_metric_total` now reports the number of metrics broken down by stability level and deprecated version

enrichment.problem: The `registered_metric_total` metric only reported a single aggregate count, providing no insight into how many metrics belong to each stability level or are deprecated, making it difficult for operators to monitor metric health and deprecation status.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and monitoring tools that scrape Kubernetes metrics (e.g., Prometheus) are affected because they receive richer metric data for analysis and alerting.
enrichment.fix: `registered_metric_total` now includes additional label dimensions for stability level and deprecated version, so the metric reports a separate count per stability tier and per deprecated version.
enrichment.impact: Operators and monitoring systems can now see the distribution of registered metrics by stability and deprecation, enabling better observability, proactive deprecation handling, and more precise alerting on metric stability trends.

feature.description: Changed `preemption_victims` metric bucket from `LinearBuckets` to `ExponentialBuckets`.
feature.author: lengrongfu
feature.userFacingChange: Change  `preemption_victims` metric bucket from `LinearBuckets` to `ExponentialBuckets`.

enrichment.problem: The `preemption_victims` metric used linear bucket boundaries, which can create high cardinality and poor resolution for a wide range of victim counts, making the metric less useful and potentially increasing monitoring overhead.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the kube-scheduler, especially any workloads that trigger pod preemption (e.g., high‑priority pods preempting lower‑priority pods).
enrichment.fix: The metric definition was changed to use exponential bucket boundaries, providing finer granularity for small values and coarser buckets for large values, reducing cardinality and improving the usefulness of the metric.
enrichment.impact: Improved observability of scheduler preemption behavior with lower memory/CPU cost for metric collection, enabling more accurate monitoring and alerting without affecting scheduler functionality.

feature.description: kubeadm: sub-phases are now able to support the dry-run mode, e.g. kubeadm reset phase cleanup-node --dry-run
feature.author: chendave

enrichment.problem: kubeadm sub-phases could not be executed with the --dry-run flag, preventing users from safely previewing actions such as node cleanup before they are applied.
enrichment.affected: Administrators using kubeadm to reset clusters or clean up nodes, especially when they want to test the command without applying changes.
enrichment.fix: Implemented dry‑run support for kubeadm sub‑phases, e.g., `kubeadm reset phase cleanup-node --dry-run`, allowing the command to run in simulation mode without making changes.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now verify the effects of kubeadm sub‑phase commands ahead of time, reducing the risk of accidental deletions or misconfigurations during cluster reset or node cleanup.

feature.description: Added alpha support for `WindowsHostNetworking` feature.
feature.author: marosset
feature.userFacingChange: Adding alpha support for WindowsHostNetworking feature

enrichment.problem: Windows pods could not use the node's network stack (host networking), limiting certain workloads and network plugin capabilities on Windows nodes.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows containers that need host network access; Windows node clusters that want to enable host networking for pods.
enrichment.fix: Introduced alpha support for the WindowsHostNetworking feature gate, enabling hostNetwork for Windows pods when the feature is enabled.
enrichment.impact: Allows Windows workloads to leverage host network interfaces, simplifying networking setups and increasing compatibility with tools that require host networking on Windows nodes.

feature.description: When `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, then `/metrics/slis` becomes available on kube-controller-manager, allowing you to scrape health check metrics.
feature.author: logicalhan
feature.userFacingChange: If `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, then `/metrics/slis` becomes available on kube-controller-manager, allowing you to scrape health check metrics.

issueContext.title: Wire up `metrics/slis` for kube-controller-manager
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

As per, https://kep.k8s.io/3466, wire up `metrics/slis` for KCM

### Why is this needed?

https://kep.k8s.io/3466

enrichment.problem: When the ComponentSLIs feature gate is disabled, the kube-controller-manager does not expose the /metrics/slis endpoint, preventing users from scraping health‑check SLI metrics for the controller manager.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-controller-manager that enable the ComponentSLIs feature gate; monitoring tools that need health‑check metrics.
enrichment.fix: Enabling the ComponentSLIs feature gate adds a new /metrics/slis endpoint to kube-controller-manager, exposing health‑check metrics that can be scraped by monitoring systems.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor controller‑manager health via standard Prometheus scrapes, improving observability and allowing early detection of degraded controller performance.

feature.description: Graduated Kubelet Device Manager to GA.
feature.author: swatisehgal
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate Kubelet Device Manager to GA.

enrichment.problem: The Kubelet Device Manager was only available as an alpha/beta feature, meaning it lacked stable APIs, default enablement, and production‑grade guarantees, limiting confidence for users needing reliable device plugin support.
enrichment.affected: Users running device plugins through the kubelet (e.g., workloads that require exclusive access to hardware devices) who previously had to enable the feature manually or work around instability.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the Kubelet Device Manager to GA. The feature is now enabled by default, its API is marked stable, version skew guarantees are provided, and documentation reflects its production‑ready status.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now rely on the device manager for device plugin workloads (e.g., GPUs, RDMA, FPGA) in production without needing feature gates. This improves stability, simplifies configuration, and encourages broader adoption of device plugins.

feature.description: In `kubeadm`, command `kubeadm join phase control-plane-prepare certs` now supports to run with `dry-run` mode on it's own.
feature.author: chendave
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: command `kubeadm join phase control-plane-prepare certs` is now supporting to run with `dry-run` mode on it's own

enrichment.problem: The `kubeadm join phase control-plane-prepare certs` subcommand could not be executed in dry-run mode, preventing users from previewing the certificate preparation steps without making changes.
enrichment.affected: Users running `kubeadm join` to add control‑plane nodes, especially those who want to test or preview the certificate preparation phase.
enrichment.fix: Added native dry-run support to the `kubeadm join phase control-plane-prepare certs` command, allowing it to run safely without applying any changes.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now validate and troubleshoot the control-plane certificate preparation step before actually joining a node, reducing risk of failed joins and improving debugging experience.

feature.description: Graduated Kubelet CPU Manager to GA.
feature.author: fromanirh
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate Kubelet CPU Manager to GA.

enrichment.problem: The CPU Manager feature in kubelet was only available as an alpha/beta feature requiring manual enablement via a feature gate, limiting its use in production environments.
enrichment.affected: Users running workloads that need static CPU allocation (e.g., guaranteed QoS pods) and administrators configuring kubelet CPU Manager.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the kubelet CPU Manager to GA, removing the feature gate requirement and making CPU pinning behavior the default stable functionality.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now rely on stable, guaranteed CPU placement for workloads that need dedicated cores (e.g., high‑performance or latency‑sensitive apps) without extra configuration, simplifying deployments and improving predictability.

feature.description: When `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, `/metrics/slis` becomes available on kube-scheduler, allowing you to scrape health check metrics.
feature.author: Richabanker
feature.userFacingChange: If `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, then `/metrics/slis` becomes available on kube-scheduler, allowing you to scrape health check metrics.

issueContext.title: Wire up metrics/slis for kube-scheduler
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

As per, https://kep.k8s.io/3466, wire up metrics/slis for KCM

### Why is this needed?

https://kep.k8s.io/3466

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler did not expose a `/metrics/slis` endpoint, so users could not scrape detailed health‑check metrics (SLIs) for the scheduler.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where users want to collect scheduler health‑check metrics; enables monitoring tools to scrape `/metrics/slis` when the feature gate is on.
enrichment.fix: When the `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, the scheduler registers the `/metrics/slis` endpoint, making SLI metrics available for scraping.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor scheduler health and performance via standard Prometheus scrapes, improving observability and enabling alerting on scheduler SLIs.

feature.description: If `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, then `/metrics/slis` becomes available on kubelet, allowing you to scrape health check metrics.
feature.author: Richabanker

issueContext.title: Wire up metrics/slis for kubelet
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

As per, https://kep.k8s.io/3466, wire up metrics/slis for kubelet

### Why is this needed?

https://kep.k8s.io/3466

enrichment.problem: When the ComponentSLIs feature gate was enabled, kubelet did not expose the `/metrics/slis` endpoint, preventing users from scraping health‑check Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics.
enrichment.affected: Users who rely on kubelet health‑check metrics for observability and alerting were unable to scrape them; enabling the endpoint resolves this.
enrichment.fix: The change adds the `/metrics/slis` endpoint to the kubelet when the ComponentSLIs gate is enabled, making health‑check metrics available for scraping.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now collect and monitor kubelet health‑check SLIs (e.g., latency, error rates) via Prometheus or other scrapers, improving visibility and reliability of node health.

feature.description: When `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, then `/metrics/slis` becomes available on `kube-proxy` allowing you to scrape health check metrics.
feature.author: Richabanker
feature.userFacingChange: If `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, then `/metrics/slis` becomes available on kube-proxy allowing you to scrape health check metrics.

issueContext.title: Wire up metrics/slis for kube-proxy
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

As per, https://kep.k8s.io/3466, wire up metrics/slis for kube-proxy

### Why is this needed?

https://kep.k8s.io/3466

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy did not expose Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics, so users could not scrape health‑check related metrics when the ComponentSLIs feature gate was enabled.
enrichment.affected: Users who enable the ComponentSLIs feature gate and rely on kube-proxy health monitoring; monitoring setups that scrape kube-proxy metrics.
enrichment.fix: When the ComponentSLIs feature gate is enabled, kube-proxy now serves a `/metrics/slis` endpoint that provides health‑check SLI metrics.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring systems (e.g., Prometheus) can now collect detailed health‑check metrics from kube-proxy, improving observability, alerting, and troubleshooting of network proxy behavior.

feature.description: Adds alpha --output plaintext protected by environment variable `KUBECTL_EXPLAIN_OPENAPIV3`
feature.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: kubectl explain only supported machine-readable output formats; users could not obtain a simple plaintext representation of OpenAPI v3 schema without custom processing.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users who run `kubectl explain` and need a human‑readable view of resource schemas.
enrichment.fix: Introduces an alpha `--output plaintext` flag for `kubectl explain`, gated behind the `KUBECTL_EXPLAIN_OPENAPIV3` environment variable, to render the OpenAPI v3 schema as human‑readable plain text.
enrichment.impact: Makes it easier for developers and operators to read and understand resource schemas directly from the CLI, improving usability for troubleshooting and learning, while keeping the feature hidden until explicitly enabled.

feature.description: Azure File CSI migration is now GA.
feature.author: andyzhangx
feature.userFacingChange: make Azure File CSI migration as GA in 1.26

enrichment.problem: Azure File storage users had to use an alpha/beta in-tree volume plugin or manually enable CSI migration, which was not considered stable or fully supported.
enrichment.affected: Users running Azure File persistent volumes via the in-tree volume plugin or who need to migrate to the Azure File CSI driver.
enrichment.fix: The Azure File CSI migration feature is promoted to General Availability in Kubernetes 1.26, making the migration path stable, default, and supported without feature gates.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now safely and seamlessly migrate Azure File volumes to the CSI driver as a stable, default behavior, improving reliability and reducing operational overhead for Azure users.

feature.description: API Server Tracing now includes a variety of new spans and span events.
feature.author: dashpole

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver tracing implementation only emitted a limited set of spans and events, making it difficult for users to get detailed observability into API requests and internal processing.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using apiserver tracing (e.g., observability platforms, cluster admins, developers troubleshooting API latency or security events) gains more detailed trace information.
enrichment.fix: Enhanced the apiserver tracing code to emit many additional spans and span events covering request handling, authentication, authorization, admission control, storage, and other phases. The new spans are integrated with the existing OpenTelemetry instrumentation.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators and developers can now obtain richer trace data from the API server, enabling finer‑grained performance debugging, latency attribution, and security/audit investigations without code changes. Observability tools that consume OpenTelemetry data will see more actionable signals.

feature.description: Added new metric `job_controller_terminated_pods_tracking_finalizer` which can be used to monitor whether the job controller is removing Pod finalizers from terminated Pods after accounting them in Job status.
feature.author: alculquicondor
feature.userFacingChange: New metric job_controller_terminated_pods_tracking_finalizer can be used to monitor whether the job controller is removing Pod finalizers from terminated Pods after accounting them in Job status.

enrichment.problem: There was no built-in metric to tell whether the job controller had successfully removed Pod finalizers from terminated Pods after they were accounted for in a Job's status, making it hard to detect cleanup issues.
enrichment.affected: Users running batch Jobs who need observability of Job controller behavior, as well as cluster admins monitoring pod lifecycle health.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the metric `job_controller_terminated_pods_tracking_finalizer` which reports the success/failure of finalizer removal for terminated Pods managed by the Job controller.
enrichment.impact: Operators and monitoring systems can now track and alert on finalizer cleanup problems for Jobs, helping to prevent stale finalizers that could block pod deletion and cause resource leaks.

feature.description: API Server tracing now includes the latency of authorization, priorityandfairness, impersonation, audit, and authentication filters.
feature.author: dashpole

enrichment.problem: The API server tracing did not capture latency of key request processing stages such as authorization, priority and fairness, impersonation, audit, and authentication filters, limiting visibility for debugging and performance analysis.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using API server tracing for observability; anyone troubleshooting API latency, especially around security and request handling components.
enrichment.fix: Extended the apiserver tracing implementation to record and expose latency metrics for the authorization, priority-and-fairness, impersonation, audit, and authentication filter stages.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can now see detailed latency breakdowns for these critical request handling steps, enabling faster root‑cause analysis of slow API calls and better observability of security‑related processing.

feature.description: '`DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver` feature is GA.'
feature.author: bertinatto
feature.userFacingChange: DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver feature is GA.

enrichment.problem: The ability for CSI drivers to handle FSGroup ownership changes was only available as a Beta feature behind the DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver feature gate, limiting its default use and causing extra configuration for users.
enrichment.affected: Users running pods that specify a securityContext.fsGroup and rely on CSI drivers that implement FSGroup delegation. Administrators no longer need to enable a beta feature gate.
enrichment.fix: The DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver feature has been graduated to General Availability (GA). The feature gate is now enabled by default, allowing kubelet to delegate FSGroup changes to CSI drivers automatically without extra flags.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use CSI drivers that support FSGroup delegation out‑of‑the‑box, simplifying security context configuration for pods that require group ownership changes and improving compatibility with storage providers.

feature.description: Updated the Lease identity naming format for the `APIServerIdentity` feature to use a persistent name.
feature.author: andrewsykim
feature.userFacingChange: Update the Lease identity naming format for the APIServerIdentity feature to use a persistent name

enrichment.problem: The Lease objects used by the APIServerIdentity feature were named with a volatile format, causing the lease name to change across API server restarts and leading to unnecessary lease churn and confusing metrics.
enrichment.affected: kube-apiserver processes that have the APIServerIdentity feature enabled; any tooling that watches the lease name will see a stable identifier.
enrichment.fix: The lease identity naming format has been updated to use a stable, persistent name, ensuring the same lease is reused for the lifetime of an API server instance.
enrichment.impact: Provides consistent leader election lease identities for the kube-apiserver, reducing noise in monitoring/alerts and improving stability of the election process.

feature.description: Metrics for `RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass` feature are now available. To see an attempt count for updating PVC retroactively with a default StorageClass see `retroactive_storageclass_total` metric and for total numer of errors see `retroactive_storageclass_errors_total`.
feature.author: RomanBednar
feature.userFacingChange: Metrics for RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass feature are now available. To see an attempt count for updating PVC retroactively with a default StorageClass see `retroactive_storageclass_total` metric and for total numer of errors see `retroactive_storageclass_errors_total`.

enrichment.problem: There were no metrics exposed for the RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass feature, so administrators could not track how many PVCs were updated retroactively with a default StorageClass or detect errors during that process.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have the RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass feature enabled, especially admins and tools that rely on storage provisioning metrics.
enrichment.fix: Added two Prometheus metrics: `retroactive_storageclass_total` (counts update attempts) and `retroactive_storageclass_errors_total` (counts errors), emitted by the controller that implements RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor the health and effectiveness of the retroactive default storageclass behavior, quickly spot failures, and assess its impact on workloads, improving observability and troubleshooting of storage provisioning.

feature.description:
Extend the job `job_finished_total metric by new `reason` label and introduce a new job metric to count pod failures
handled by pod failure policy with respect to the action applied.
feature.author: mimowo
feature.userFacingChange:
Extend the job `job_finished_total metric by new `reason` label and introduce a new job metric to count pod failures
handled by pod failure policy with respect to the action applied.

enrichment.problem: Job monitoring lacked granularity: the existing job_finished_total metric did not indicate why a Job finished, and there was no metric for pod failures handled by the pod failure policy, making it hard to observe and diagnose failure reasons and policy actions.
enrichment.affected: Users of Jobs who rely on Prometheus metrics for monitoring job lifecycle and pod failure handling; also any tooling that consumes these metrics.
enrichment.fix: The Job controller now adds a `reason` label to the `job_finished_total` metric, and introduces a new metric that counts pod failures processed by the pod failure policy, labeled by the action taken (e.g., fail, retry).
enrichment.impact: Operators can now see why Jobs completed (success, backoff limit exceeded, etc.) and how pod failure policies are applied, enabling finer‑grained alerting, debugging, and capacity planning for batch workloads.

feature.description: '`RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass` feature is now beta.'
feature.author: RomanBednar
feature.userFacingChange: RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass feature is now beta.

enrichment.problem: Previously, marking a StorageClass as the default only affected newly created PersistentVolumeClaims; existing PVCs without a storageClassName were left unbound, requiring manual updates.
enrichment.affected: Users with existing PersistentVolumeClaims that did not specify a storageClassName and rely on default storage class behavior.
enrichment.fix: The RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass feature is promoted to beta, enabling the storage‑class controller to retroactively bind existing PVCs that lack a storageClassName to the default StorageClass when it is set.
enrichment.impact: Clusters automatically apply the default StorageClass to both new and existing PVCs, simplifying storage provisioning and preventing orphaned PVCs, which improves operational reliability for workloads that rely on default storage.

feature.description:
'`CSIMigrationvSphere` was upgraded to GA and locked to true. Do not upgrade to K8s
1.26 if you need Windows, or XFS, or raw block support until vSphere CSI Driver
adds support for them in a version post v2.7.x.'
feature.author: divyenpatel
feature.userFacingChange: CSIMigrationvSphere upgraded to GA and locked to true. Do not upgrade to K8s 1.26 if you need Windows, or XFS, or raw block support until vSphere CSI Driver adds support for them in a version post v2.7.x.

enrichment.problem: CSIMigrationvSphere feature was promoted to GA and permanently enabled (locked to true) in Kubernetes 1.26. The vSphere CSI driver version 2.7.x does not yet support Windows workloads, XFS file system, or raw block volumes, so those capabilities become unavailable after upgrading.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the vSphere CSI driver (≤ v2.7.x) with Windows workloads, XFS file system volumes, or raw block volume support.
enrichment.fix: The change itself makes CSIMigrationvSphere always true. Users who require Windows nodes, XFS storage, or raw block volumes must postpone upgrading to Kubernetes 1.26 until a later vSphere CSI driver release adds support for those features.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on Windows pods, XFS-backed PersistentVolumes, or raw block volume provisioning cannot safely upgrade to v1.26, leading to potential upgrade delays and operational inconvenience.

feature.description: If `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, then `/metrics/slis` now becomes available on cloud-controller-manager allowing you to scrape health check metrics.
feature.author: Richabanker
feature.userFacingChange: If `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, then `/metrics/slis` becomes available on cloud-controller-manager allowing you to scrape health check metrics.

issueContext.title: Wire up metrics/slis for cloud-controller-manager
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

As per, https://kep.k8s.io/3466, wire up metrics/slis for ccm

### Why is this needed?

https://kep.k8s.io/3466

enrichment.problem: Cloud-controller-manager did not expose health check metrics via a dedicated endpoint, preventing users from scraping detailed health SLI data when the ComponentSLIs feature gate is enabled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running cloud-controller-manager with the ComponentSLIs feature gate enabled, particularly cloud provider integrations that rely on health monitoring.
enrichment.fix: When the ComponentSLIs feature gate is turned on, the cloud-controller-manager now serves a `/metrics/slis` endpoint that provides health check metrics for scraping.
enrichment.impact: Enables better observability and monitoring of cloud-controller-manager health, allowing operators to integrate these metrics into alerting and dashboards and improve reliability of cloud provider integrations.

feature.description: The `ProxyTerminatingEndpoints` feature is now Beta and enabled by default. When enabled, kube-proxy will attempt to route traffic to terminating pods when the traffic policy is `Local` and there are only terminating pods remaining on a node.
feature.author: andrewsykim
feature.userFacingChange: The ProxyTerminatingEndpoints feature is now Beta and enabled by default. When enabled, kube-proxy will attempt to route traffic to terminating pods when the traffic policy is Local and there are only terminating pods remaining on a node.

enrichment.problem: When a Service has trafficPolicy=Local and all pods on a node are terminating, kube-proxy would stop routing traffic to that node, causing a temporary loss of service availability.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Services with trafficPolicy=Local where pods are being terminated on a node, particularly those that experienced traffic blackholing during shutdown.
enrichment.fix: The ProxyTerminatingEndpoints feature is promoted to Beta and enabled by default. kube-proxy now includes terminating pods as valid endpoints when they are the only pods left on a node and the Service trafficPolicy is Local.
enrichment.impact: Service traffic remains uninterrupted during pod termination, reducing connection drops and improving reliability for workloads that rely on Local traffic routing.

feature.description: Promoting `WindowsHostProcessContainers` to stable.
feature.author: marosset
feature.userFacingChange: Promoting WindowsHostProcessContainers to stable

enrichment.problem: Windows host process containers were only available behind an Alpha/Beta feature gate, limiting their use in production and requiring extra configuration.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows workloads that need host‑process containers on Windows nodes.
enrichment.fix: The WindowsHostProcessContainers feature is promoted to Stable, removing the feature gate requirement and guaranteeing ongoing support in the core release.
enrichment.impact: Clusters running Windows workloads can now use host process containers in production without special flags, simplifying deployment and improving reliability for privileged Windows containers.

feature.description:
'Pod Security admission: the pod-security `warn` level will now default to
the `enforce` level.'
feature.author: tallclair
feature.userFacingChange: Pod Security admission: the pod-security `warn` level will now default to the `enforce` level.

enrichment.problem: When the pod-security admission controller was set to the `warn` level, it only emitted warnings and allowed pods that violated policies. Users relying on this behavior could unintentionally run non‑compliant workloads.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with Pod Security admission enabled and the `warn` level configured. Workloads that previously passed with warnings will now be blocked.
enrichment.fix: The default action for the `warn` level is changed to behave like `enforce`; pods that violate the configured Pod Security Standards will now be rejected instead of merely warned.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use the `warn` level will start rejecting non‑compliant pods, improving security posture. Administrators may need to update policies or be prepared for pod creation failures that previously succeeded with only a warning.

feature.description: '`NodeOutOfServiceVolumeDetach` is now beta.'
feature.author: xing-yang
feature.userFacingChange: NodeOutOfServiceVolumeDetach is now beta.

enrichment.problem: When a node was marked OutOfService, volumes attached to that node were not automatically detached, requiring manual cleanup and potentially leaving orphaned volumes.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and workloads that rely on CSI volume attachments when nodes are taken out of service, especially during node maintenance or scaling down.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the NodeOutOfServiceVolumeDetach feature, now graduated to beta, which automatically detaches CSI volumes from a node when it enters the OutOfService state.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies node decommissioning and improves storage resource hygiene, reducing manual steps and preventing orphaned volume issues for clusters using CSI drivers.

feature.description: Adds metrics `force_delete_pods_total` and `force_delete_pod_errors_total` in the Pod GC Controller.
feature.author: xing-yang

enrichment.problem: There were no exposed metrics for tracking when the Pod Garbage Collector force-deletes pods or encounters errors during those deletions, making it difficult for operators to monitor and alert on this behavior.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and monitoring systems that rely on metrics from the Pod Garbage Collector; the change is relevant when pods are force-deleted due to GC constraints.
enrichment.fix: Adds two new Prometheus metrics—`force_delete_pods_total` (counts successful forced deletions) and `force_delete_pod_errors_total` (counts errors encountered during forced deletions)—to the Pod GC controller in kube-controller-manager.
enrichment.impact: Provides operators with observability into forced pod deletions, enabling better monitoring, alerting, and troubleshooting of garbage collection issues, which improves cluster reliability and debugging capabilities.

feature.description: Added publishing events when enabling/disabling `TopologyAwareHints`.
feature.author: LiorLieberman
feature.userFacingChange: Added: publishing events when enabling/disabling topologyAwareHints.

enrichment.problem: There were no events emitted when the TopologyAwareHints feature was turned on or off, making it hard for operators to track changes and debug scheduling behavior.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the scheduler's TopologyAwareHints feature, especially administrators and monitoring systems that need visibility into hint configuration changes.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now publishes Kubernetes events whenever TopologyAwareHints is enabled or disabled, providing observable signals for the change.
enrichment.impact: Operators and monitoring tools can now see when TopologyAwareHints is toggled, improving observability, troubleshooting, and integration with alerting pipelines.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.3.
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss upstream security fixes, bug fixes, and performance improvements provided by newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with Go 1.19.3.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.19.3, recompiling all components with the newer compiler and standard library.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components receive the latest Go runtime security patches and performance improvements, reducing the risk of compiler‑related bugs and ensuring compatibility with newer Go ecosystem tooling.

feature.description: Added reconstruction of SELinux mount context after kubelet restart. Feature `SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod` is now fully implemented and kubelet does not lose its cache of SELinux contexts after kubelet process restart.
feature.author: jsafrane
feature.userFacingChange: Added reconstruction of SELinux mount context after kubelet restart. Feature SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod is now fully implemented and kubelet does not lose its cache of SELinux contexts after kubelet process restart.

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet process restarts, it discards its cached SELinux mount contexts, causing SELinux relabeling to be lost for volumes that rely on the SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that rely on SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod (pods using SELinux‑enabled volumes) on nodes where the kubelet may be restarted.
enrichment.fix: Implemented reconstruction of SELinux mount context after kubelet restart, completing the SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature so the kubelet retains or rebuilds its SELinux context cache automatically.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use SELinux labeling on their volumes will no longer encounter SELinux permission errors after a kubelet restart, improving security enforcement and stability for SELinux‑enabled clusters.

feature.description: Added alpha support for returning container and pod metrics from CRI, instead of cAdvsior.
feature.author: haircommander
feature.userFacingChange: Add alpha support for returning container and pod metrics from CRI, instead of cAdvsior

enrichment.problem: cAdvisor was the only source for container and pod metrics; CRI implementations could not provide metrics, limiting observability and future deprecation of cAdvisor.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the metrics API (e.g., metrics-server) and any node runtimes that rely on CRI; primarily affects kubelet behavior.
enrichment.fix: Alpha implementation in the kubelet that queries container and pod metrics via the CRI instead of cAdvisor, exposing them through the metrics API.
enrichment.impact: Allows metrics providers to obtain data directly from the container runtime, improves consistency across runtimes, and paves the way for eventual removal of cAdvisor.

feature.description:
'Promoted the `APIServerIdentity` feature to Beta. By default, each `kube-apiserver`
will now create a Lease in the `kube-system` namespace. These lease objects can
be used to identify the number of active API servers in the cluster, and may also
be used for future features such as the Storage Version API.'
feature.author: andrewsykim
feature.userFacingChange: Promote the `APIServerIdentity` feature to Beta. By default, each kube-apiserver will now create a Lease in the `kube-system` namespace. These lease objects can be used to identify the number of active API servers in the cluster, and may also be used for future features such as the Storage Version API.

enrichment.problem: There was no built‑in way to discover how many kube‑apiserver instances are running in a cluster, making HA monitoring and future features that need API server identity difficult.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes control‑plane clusters, especially those running multiple API server replicas; administrators and monitoring tools that need API server identity.
enrichment.fix: The APIServerIdentity feature is promoted to Beta and is enabled by default. Each kube‑apiserver now creates a Lease object in the kube‑system namespace, representing its identity and liveness.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators and tooling can read the Lease objects to count active API servers, improving HA observability and enabling upcoming features such as the Storage Version API that depend on knowing which API servers are alive.

feature.description: kubectl shell completions for the bash shell now include descriptions.
feature.author: marckhouzam

enrichment.problem: Bash shell completion for kubectl did not provide inline descriptions of commands and flags, forcing users to look up documentation to understand their purpose.
enrichment.affected: All users running kubectl with Bash shell completion are affected; they will now see descriptive help in the auto‑complete suggestions.
enrichment.fix: The bash completion script for kubectl is updated to embed descriptive text for each command and flag, so `kubectl <TAB>` now shows helpful explanations alongside completion options.
enrichment.impact: Improves usability and productivity for developers and operators who rely on bash autocompletion, reducing context switches to documentation and lowering the chance of misusing flags.

feature.description: CLI flag `pod-eviction-timeout` is deprecated and will be removed together with `enable-taint-manager` in v1.27.
feature.author: kerthcet

enrichment.problem: The kubelet CLI flags `pod-eviction-timeout` and `enable-taint-manager` are deprecated and will be removed in v1.27, which can cause kubelet startup failures for clusters that still use these flags.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that configure kubelet with `pod-eviction-timeout` or `enable-taint-manager` flags.
enrichment.fix: The flags have been removed; users must stop using them and rely on the default behavior or alternative configuration options before upgrading to v1.27.
enrichment.impact: Administrators need to update their kubelet startup scripts and configuration to remove the deprecated flags to avoid breakage during upgrade.

feature.description: Updated cAdvisor to v0.46.0.
feature.author: bobbypage

enrichment.problem: Older cAdvisor version (pre‑v0.46.0) could miss or misreport container resource usage metrics, limiting accurate monitoring.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet on all nodes that report metrics; any workloads that rely on cAdvisor metrics (e.g., HorizontalPodAutoscaler, Prometheus).
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now bundles cAdvisor v0.46.0, which includes bug fixes, performance improvements, and updated metric collection.
enrichment.impact: Improved reliability of node‑level and pod‑level metrics used by dashboards, autoscalers, and monitoring tools.

feature.description: Promoted `kubectl alpha events` to `kubectl events`.
feature.author: soltysh
feature.userFacingChange: Promote kubectl alpha events to kubectl events

enrichment.problem: Users had to use the alpha command `kubectl alpha events` to view cluster events, which required the alpha flag and lacked the stability and discoverability of a regular command.
enrichment.affected: All kubectl users who query or monitor events in a cluster, especially scripts and automation that relied on the alpha command.
enrichment.fix: The alpha command has been promoted to a stable, top‑level command `kubectl events`, making it part of the regular CLI without the alpha prefix.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies event inspection for all kubectl users, encourages broader usage, and aligns the command with the stable CLI surface, reducing confusion and improving tooling consistency.

apiChange.description: Added a kube-proxy flag (`--iptables-localhost-nodeports`, default true) to allow disabling NodePort services on loopback addresses. Note: this only applies to iptables mode and ipv4.
apiChange.author: cyclinder
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add a kube-proxy flag (--iptables-localhost-nodeports, default true) to allow disabling NodePort services on loopback addresses. Note: this only applies to iptables mode and ipv4.

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy had no way to prevent NodePort services from being bound to the loopback interface in iptables mode on IPv4, causing NodePort traffic to be reachable locally on the node.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-proxy in iptables mode on IPv4 where NodePort services might be unintentionally reachable via 127.0.0.1 on the node.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new kube-proxy flag `--iptables-localhost-nodeports` (default true). When set to false, kube-proxy stops creating iptables rules that expose NodePort services on the node's loopback addresses.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can now disable localhost access to NodePort services, reducing accidental local exposure and improving node‑level security posture for IPv4 clusters using iptables mode.

apiChange.description: Enabled `kube-controller-manager` to support '--concurrent-horizontal-pod-autoscaler-syncs' flag to set the number of horizontal pod autoscaler controller workers.
apiChange.author: zroubalik
apiChange.userFacingChange: kube-controller-manager supports '--concurrent-horizontal-pod-autoscaler-syncs' flag to set the number of horizontal pod autoscaler controller workers.

issueContext.title: HPA scheduling implementation doesn't scale well with custom/external metrics - all checks are sequential by one goroutine
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
I created an external metric that took roughly 100ms; then to see what happened if there were many of them, I created 1,000 HPAs using it.  Usually every HPA checks every 15s, but this resulted in each HPA check checking every 120 seconds - a drift/delay of over 100 seconds.

**What you expected to happen**:

- Each HPA with a custom/external metric should only drift by maximum 100ms every 15s or delay a second every 3-5 minutes
- Other HPAs not using custom/external metrics should not be impacted by duration of custom/external metrics
- The quantity of deployments with HPAs should not degrade each HPAs ability to respond to signals requiring scaling up (spikes e.g.)

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
* Create and install the https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/custom-metrics-apiserver and alter its code to add a delay in the `GetExternalMetric` method of the [Testing Provider](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/custom-metrics-apiserver/blob/master/test-adapter/provider/provider.go#L327)
* Also add logging to the method with timestamps [logrus](https://github.com/Sirupsen/logrus) supports timestamps, e.g.
* Create 1,000 HPA objects referring to that test metric - possibly 1,000 deployments as well, but one will work fine too even if not a _real_ use case.
* Pick one of your HPA's and watch for the time between its call to `GetExternalMetric`.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```bash
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"19", GitVersion:"v1.19.2", GitCommit:"f5743093fd1c663cb0cbc89748f730662345d44d", GitTreeState:"clean",

enrichment.problem: HorizontalPodAutoscaler controller processed all metrics sequentially with a single goroutine, causing large delays (e.g., 120s vs 15s) when many HPAs used custom/external metrics.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running large numbers of HorizontalPodAutoscaler objects, particularly those using custom or external metrics, and the workloads they control.
enrichment.fix: kube-controller-manager now accepts the '--concurrent-horizontal-pod-autoscaler-syncs' flag to configure multiple HPA controller workers, enabling parallel metric processing.
enrichment.impact: Reduces scaling latency and improves responsiveness of HPAs, especially in clusters with many HPAs or external/custom metrics, preventing scaling drifts.

apiChange.description: `kubectl wait` command with `jsonpath` flag will wait for target path until timeout.
apiChange.author: jonyhy96
apiChange.userFacingChange: kubectl wait command with jsonpath flag will wait for target path appear until timeout.

enrichment.problem: `kubectl wait` did not honor the `--for=jsonpath=...` flag; it returned immediately instead of waiting for the specified JSON path to appear, causing scripts that relied on this behavior to fail or proceed prematurely.
enrichment.affected: Any user or automation that uses `kubectl wait` with the `--for=jsonpath=` flag to wait for a field to appear in a resource.
enrichment.fix: The `kubectl wait` implementation was updated to monitor the target JSONPath expression and block until the field becomes present (or the timeout expires).
enrichment.impact: Users can now reliably wait for arbitrary object fields to materialize, improving automation scripts, CI pipelines, and operational tooling that depend on `kubectl wait` for state verification.

apiChange.description:
'Added a `ResourceClaim` API (in the `resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1` API group and
behind the `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature gate).
The new API is now more flexible than the existing Device Plugins feature of Kubernetes because it
allows Pods to request (claim) special kinds of resources, which can be available at node level, cluster
level, or following any other model you implement.'
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Add a `ResourceClaim` API (in the resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1 API group and
behind the `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature gate).
The new API is more flexible than the existing Device Plugins feature of Kubernetes because it
allows Pods to request (claim) special kinds of resources, which can be available at node level, cluster
level, or following any other model you implement.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes did not have a generic way for Pods to request special resources beyond the limited Device Plugins mechanism, restricting flexibility for custom resource allocation models.
enrichment.affected: Pods that need custom or special resources and cluster administrators who want to expose such resources to workloads.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `ResourceClaim` API in the `resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1` group, gated by `DynamicResourceAllocation`. Pods can now create and reference ResourceClaims to request resources that may be provided at node level, cluster level, or via custom implementations.
enrichment.impact: Enables users and platform developers to define and claim arbitrary resources for workloads, improving resource scheduling, supporting new hardware or software resource types, and reducing reliance on the older device plugin model.

apiChange.description:
Add auth API to get self subject attributes (new selfsubjectreviews API is added). 
The corresponding command for kubctl is provided - `kubectl auth whoami`.
apiChange.author: nabokihms
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Add auth API to get self subject attributes (new selfsubjectreviews API is added). 
The corresponding command for kubctl is provided - `kubectl auth whoami`.

enrichment.problem: Previously there was no API or kubectl command for a user to retrieve their own subject attributes (e.g., groups, scopes) from the control plane, making it hard to introspect identity or debug RBAC issues.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes users and administrators who need to discover their own authentication attributes, including scripts and CI pipelines that interact with the API.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new SelfSubjectReview API and the corresponding `kubectl auth whoami` command that returns the caller's subject attributes, enabling users and scripts to query their own identity information directly.
enrichment.impact: Provides a simple, reliable way to view the current user's attributes, aiding debugging of RBAC, improving automation scripts, and enhancing security auditing by letting users verify their effective identity without needing elevated permissions.

apiChange.description: Kubelet external Credential Provider feature is moved to GA. Credential Provider Plugin and Credential Provider Config APIs updated from `v1beta1` to `v1` with no API changes.
apiChange.author: ndixita
apiChange.userFacingChange: Kubelet external Credential Provider feature is moved to GA. Credential Provider Plugin and Credential Provider Config APIs updated from v1beta1 to v1 with no API changes.

enrichment.problem: The external Credential Provider feature was only available as a beta API (v1beta1), limiting its stability guarantee and requiring users to track a beta version.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubelet with external credential provider plugins, and any workload that relies on those plugins for image pull or other authentication needs.
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted to GA. The Credential Provider Plugin and Credential Provider Config APIs are moved from v1beta1 to the stable v1 version, without any functional changes.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use the external credential provider (e.g., for pulling images from private registries) now have a stable, GA‑supported API. Existing configurations continue to work, but new deployments should reference the v1 API. This improves reliability and reduces churn for users.

apiChange.description:
Introduce `v1beta3` for Priority and Fairness with the following changes to the API spec:
- rename 'assuredConcurrencyShares' (located under `spec.limited') to 'nominalConcurrencyShares'.
- apply strategic merge patch annotations to 'Conditions' of flowschemas and `prioritylevelconfigurations`.
apiChange.author: tkashem
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Introduce v1beta3 for Priority and Fairness with the following changes to the API spec:
- rename 'assuredConcurrencyShares' (located under spec.limited') to 'nominalConcurrencyShares'
- apply strategic merge patch annotations to 'Conditions' of flowschemas and prioritylevelconfigurations

issueContext.title: Add patch annotations to APF API types in next version
flowschemas resource is currently skipped by TestApplyResetFields test.
issueContext.body:
#### What happened:
`flowschemas` resource is currently skipped by `TestApplyResetFields` test.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/integration/apiserver/apply/reset_fields_test.go#L70-L74
```
var resetFieldsSkippedResources = map[string]struct{}{
	// TODO: flowschemas is flaking,
	// possible bug in the flowschemas controller.
	"flowschemas": {},
}
```

When it flakes, it fails with the following error
```
 reset_fields_test.go:288: expected conflict, got error <nil>
```

this is the test result:
```
--- FAIL: TestApplyResetFields (5.94s)
    --- FAIL: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2,_Resource=flowschemas (0.05s)
    --- PASS: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta2,_Resource=prioritylevelconfigurations (0.01s)
    --- FAIL: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1,_Resource=flowschemas (0.01s)
    --- PASS: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1,_Resource=prioritylevelconfigurations (0.01s)
    --- PASS: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1alpha1,_Resource=flowschemas (0.01s)
    --- PASS: TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1alpha1,_Resource=prioritylevelconfigurations (0.01s)
```


#### What you expected to happen:

We need to identify the root case of why it flakes and fix it. "flowschemas" being skipped means that we may not catch any errors related to field resetting when we add a new version of the API.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
- remove "flowschemas" from `resetFieldsSkippedResources`
- go test -v -count=1 ./test/integration/apiserver/apply -run="TestApplyResetFields/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io"

run multiple times to see the flake

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):

enrichment.problem: The FlowSchemaStatus and PriorityLevelConfigurationStatus condition slices lacked the strategic merge patch annotations (patchStrategy and patchMergeKey), causing apply/patch operations to misbehave and leading to test flakiness. Additionally, the field name 'assuredConcurrencyShares' was inconsistent with the spec and required renaming.
enrichment.affected: Users and controllers that interact with the Priority and Fairness API (FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration), especially those using kubectl apply or strategic merge patch.
enrichment.fix: Introduce a new v1beta3 version of the Priority and Fairness API that (1) renames spec.limited.assuredConcurrencyShares to spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares, and (2) adds the required strategic merge patch annotations to the Conditions slices of FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration resources.
enrichment.impact: Clients can now safely use strategic merge patch and server-side apply on FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration objects without unexpected conflicts. The API becomes more consistent, and the apply reset fields test is no longer flaky, improving overall reliability of the flow-control subsystem.

apiChange.description:
'Kubelet added the following Pod failure conditions:
- `DisruptionTarget` (graceful node shutdown, node pressure eviction)'
apiChange.author: mimowo
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Kubelet adds the following pod failure conditions:
- DisruptionTarget (graceful node shutdown, node pressure eviction)

enrichment.problem: Pods terminated during a graceful node shutdown or node pressure eviction did not have a specific failure condition, so controllers and users could not distinguish these disruptions from other pod failures, leading to unnecessary restarts or retries.
enrichment.affected: Pods that are terminated because of graceful node shutdowns or node pressure evictions; workloads managed by controllers such as Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, etc.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now adds a new PodFailureCondition called `DisruptionTarget` to pods that are being terminated because of a graceful node shutdown or node pressure eviction.
enrichment.impact: Controllers (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets) and applications can now detect that a pod termination was due to node disruption, allowing them to avoid unnecessary pod recreation and improve observability of node‑related failures.

apiChange.description: Add `percentageOfNodesToScore` as a scheduler profile level parameter to API version `v1`. When a profile `percentageOfNodesToScore` is set, it will override global `percentageOfNodesToScore`.
apiChange.author: yuanchen8911
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add percentageOfNodesToScore as a scheduler profile level parameter to API version v1. If a profile percentageOfNodesToScore is set, it will override global percentageOfNodesToScore.

enrichment.problem: The scheduler API only allowed a single global `percentageOfNodesToScore` setting, preventing different scheduler profiles from using tailored node‑scoring percentages.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use multiple scheduler profiles and need different node‑scoring percentages per profile.
enrichment.fix: Added a `percentageOfNodesToScore` field to the SchedulerProfile spec in the v1 API. When set on a profile, it overrides the global setting for that profile.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can now tune the node‑scoring fraction per profile, improving scheduling latency and allowing more granular performance optimization for workloads that use different profiles.

apiChange.description: Added a feature that allows a `StatefulSet` to start numbering replicas from an arbitrary non-negative ordinal, using the `.spec.ordinals.start` field.
apiChange.author: pwschuurman
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added a feature that allows a StatefulSet to start numbering replicas from an arbitrary non-negative ordinal, using the `.spec.ordinals.start` field.

enrichment.problem: StatefulSets could only start replica numbering at ordinal 0, making it difficult to migrate or integrate workloads that required a different starting index or to avoid naming collisions.
enrichment.affected: Users deploying or managing StatefulSets that need custom ordinal numbering, such as migration scenarios or services relying on specific pod names.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the optional `.spec.ordinals.start` field in the StatefulSet spec, allowing users to specify any non‑negative integer as the first replica ordinal.
enrichment.impact: Enables seamless migration of existing stateful workloads, custom naming schemes, and better integration with external systems that expect specific pod ordinal numbers, reducing manual work and potential errors.

apiChange.description: Moved `MixedProtocolLBService` from beta to GA.
apiChange.author: janosi
apiChange.userFacingChange: Moving MixedProtocolLBService from beta to GA

enrichment.problem: The MixedProtocolLBService type was only available as a beta feature, requiring a feature gate and lacking guaranteed long‑term support.
enrichment.affected: Users who rely on or plan to use MixedProtocolLBService (service type) in their workloads, as well as clusters that need a stable load‑balancer service for mixed protocol traffic.
enrichment.fix: MixedProtocolLBService has been graduated to GA. The service type is now stable, no longer requires a feature gate, and is fully supported by the API server and cloud‑controller manager.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use MixedProtocolLBService in production without feature‑gate gymnastics, gaining stable behavior and guaranteed support. Existing beta usage continues to work unchanged.

apiChange.description: Added a `--topology-manager-policy-options` flag to the kubelet to support fine tuning the topology manager policies. The first policy option, `prefer-closest-numa-nodes`, allows these policies to favor sets of NUMA nodes with shorter distance between nodes when making admission decisions.
apiChange.author: PiotrProkop
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added a --topology-manager-policy-options flag to the kubelet to support fine tuning the topology manager policies. The first policy option, `prefer-closest-numa-nodes`, allows these policies to favor sets of NUMA nodes with shorter distance between nodes when making admission decisions.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet topology manager policies could not be fine‑tuned, and there was no way to prefer NUMA node sets that are physically closer, limiting performance optimization for NUMA‑aware workloads.
enrichment.affected: Users running NUMA‑aware workloads that rely on the topology manager for pod resource allocation. The change also benefits cluster operators who want more control over pod placement on multi‑NUMA nodes.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `--topology-manager-policy-options` flag in the kubelet. The first option, `prefer-closest-numa-nodes`, lets the topology manager favor sets of NUMA nodes with shorter distances when making admission decisions.
enrichment.impact: Allows cluster operators and workload developers to improve pod performance on NUMA hardware by reducing memory latency and improving cache locality, leading to more efficient resource usage and potentially higher throughput for latency‑sensitive applications.

apiChange.description: Aggregated discovery will be alpha and can be toggled with the `AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint` feature flag.
apiChange.author: Jefftree
apiChange.userFacingChange: Yes, aggregated discovery will be alpha and can be toggled with the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature flag

enrichment.problem: Clusters lacked a unified discovery endpoint for aggregated API servers, requiring clients to make separate discovery calls for each aggregated API.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or tooling that performs API discovery, especially those interacting with aggregated API servers, when the feature gate is enabled.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint, an alpha‑level discovery endpoint that can be enabled via the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature gate, allowing a single discovery request to return both built‑in and aggregated API resources.
enrichment.impact: Clients (e.g., kubectl, client‑go) can retrieve a complete API surface with one request, simplifying client code and reducing network round‑trips. Enables early testing of aggregated discovery in clusters that enable the feature flag.

apiChange.description: Added a new namespace alpha field to `DataSourceRef` field in `PersistentVolumeClaim` API.
apiChange.author: ttakahashi21
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add a new namespace alpha field to dataSourceRef field in PersistentVolumeClaim API.

enrichment.problem: PVCs could only reference a data source (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot) in the same namespace, preventing users from using snapshots or other data sources across namespaces.
enrichment.affected: Users creating PersistentVolumeClaims that rely on a data source (such as VolumeSnapshots) located in a different namespace.
enrichment.fix: Introduced an optional alpha `namespace` field on the `dataSourceRef` of a PersistentVolumeClaim, allowing a PVC to specify the namespace of the referenced data source.
enrichment.impact: Enables cross‑namespace snapshot and other data‑source usage, paving the way for richer storage workflows and future CSI features without requiring work‑arounds.

apiChange.description: New Pod API field `.spec.schedulingGates` is introduced to enable users to control when to mark a Pod as scheduling ready.
apiChange.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: Users could not control when a Pod is considered scheduling‑ready, making it difficult to delay scheduling until certain conditions (e.g., init containers, sidecars) are satisfied.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that need to postpone scheduling, such as Pods with init containers, sidecar injection, or custom controllers that set scheduling gates.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the .spec.schedulingGates field in the Pod API. Pods with pending scheduling gates are excluded from the scheduler until all gates are removed, allowing explicit control over scheduling readiness.
enrichment.impact: Enables workloads to reliably defer scheduling, improving coordination of multi‑container setups and custom controllers without needing work‑arounds.

apiChange.description:
'A new `preEnqueue` extension point was added to scheduler's component config
`v1beta2/v1beta3/v1`.'
apiChange.author: Huang-Wei
apiChange.userFacingChange: A new `preEnqueue` extension point is added to scheduler's component config v1beta2/v1beta3/v1.

enrichment.problem: Scheduler configuration did not provide a hook to run custom logic before a pod is enqueued, limiting plugin extensibility for pre‑enqueue processing such as validation or mutation.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the kube-scheduler and custom scheduler plugins that need to run logic before pods are enqueued.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `preEnqueue` extension point in the scheduler's component config (v1beta2, v1beta3, v1), allowing scheduler plugins to execute code before a pod is placed onto the scheduling queue.
enrichment.impact: Enables developers to add custom pre‑enqueue checks or transformations, expanding scheduler plugin capabilities and giving clusters finer control over pod admission into the scheduling pipeline.

apiChange.description: Introduced `v1alpha1` API for validating admission policies, enabling extensible admission control via CEL expressions (KEP  3488: CEL for Admission Control). To use, enable the `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` feature gate and the `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1` API via `--runtime-config`.
apiChange.author: cici37
apiChange.userFacingChange: Introduce v1alpha1 API for validating admission policies, enabling extensible admission control via CEL expressions (KEP  3488: CEL for Admission Control). To use, enable the `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` feature gate and the `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1` API via `--runtime-config`.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes lacked a native, extensible way to define validating admission policies using expressive CEL expressions, limiting custom admission control capabilities.
enrichment.affected: Users who need custom admission validation (cluster admins, developers) and any workloads subject to new validation policies.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1 API for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, enabled via the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy feature gate and runtime-config, allowing administrators to write admission validation logic with CEL.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now implement flexible, fine‑grained admission validation rules without custom webhooks, simplifying policy management and improving security posture.

apiChange.description: The `EndpointSliceTerminatingCondition` feature gate was graduated to GA. The gate is now locked and will be removed in v1.28.
apiChange.author: andrewsykim
apiChange.userFacingChange: The EndpointSliceTerminatingCondition feature gate has graduated to GA. The gate is now locked and will be removed in v1.28.

enrichment.problem: The EndpointSliceTerminatingCondition feature gate was previously behind a flag, requiring users to enable it manually. This caused extra configuration and potential confusion, especially as the feature was effectively stable.
enrichment.affected: Administrators who enabled the EndpointSliceTerminatingCondition feature gate and any workloads relying on custom endpoint termination behavior. Also affects clusters that have the flag set in component configs (kube-apiserver, controller-manager).
enrichment.fix: The feature gate has been graduated to GA, the flag is now locked (always enabled) and will be removed in v1.28, eliminating the need for manual gating.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to set the EndpointSliceTerminatingCondition flag. Existing configurations that reference the flag will need to be cleaned up before v1.28 to avoid startup errors. The GA status ensures the terminating condition on EndpointSlices is consistently available, improving reliability of service endpoint handling.

apiChange.description: Enable the "Retriable and non-retriable pod failures for jobs" feature into beta.
apiChange.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: Jobs could not distinguish between retriable and non-retriable pod failures, causing all pod failures to be treated the same way (typically triggering a retry), which made it difficult to stop a job after a definitive failure.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses the Job API (e.g., batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, cron jobs) and needs fine‑grained control over retry behavior.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a beta feature that adds explicit pod failure classifications for Jobs: retriable failures (which cause the Job controller to create a replacement pod) and non‑retriable failures (which mark the Job as failed without further retries). The feature is gated and enabled by default in this release.
