enrichment.impact: Users can now define more precise failure handling for batch workloads, preventing endless retry loops and reducing resource waste. This improves reliability and predictability of Job‑based processing pipelines.

apiChange.description:
'`PodDisruptionBudget` now adds an alpha `spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` field.
When the `PDBUnhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` feature-gate is enabled in `kube-apiserver`,
setting this field to `"AlwaysAllow"` allows pods to be evicted if they do not
have a ready condition, regardless of whether the PodDisruptionBudget is currently
healthy.'
apiChange.author: atiratree
apiChange.userFacingChange: PodDisruptionBudget adds an alpha `spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` field. When the `PDBUnhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` feature-gate is enabled in `kube-apiserver`, setting this field to `"AlwaysAllow"` allows pods to be evicted if they do not have a ready condition, regardless of whether the PodDisruptionBudget is currently healthy.

enrichment.problem: When a PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) is in place, pods that are not Ready are prevented from being evicted even if they are unhealthy, which can block node drains or other maintenance operations.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use PodDisruptionBudgets and need to evict pods that are not Ready, such as during node drains or upgrades.
enrichment.fix: Introduces an alpha field `spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` on PDBs. When the `PDBUnhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` feature gate is enabled, setting this field to `"AlwaysAllow"` permits eviction of pods without a Ready condition regardless of the PDB's overall health.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now safely evict unhealthy pods during maintenance without being blocked by a healthy PDB, improving node lifecycle handling and reducing disruption risk.

apiChange.description:
'Priority and Fairness has introduced a new feature called _borrowing_ that allows an API priority level
to borrow a number of seats from other priority level(s). As a cluster operator, you can enable borrowing
for a certain priority level configuration object via the two newly introduced fields `lendablePercent`, and
`borrowingLimitPercent` located under the `.spec.limited` field of the designated priority level.
This change added the following metrics:
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_nominal_limit_seats`: Nominal number of execution seats configured for each priority level
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_lower_limit_seats`: Configured lower bound on number of execution seats available to each priority level
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_upper_limit_seats`: Configured upper bound on number of execution seats available to each priority level
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats`: Observations, at the end of every nanosecond, of (the number of seats each priority level could use) / (nominal number of seats for that level)
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats_high_watermark`: High watermark, over last adjustment period, of demand_seats
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats_average`: Time-weighted average, over last adjustment period, of demand_seats
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats_stdev`: Time-weighted standard deviation, over last adjustment period, of demand_seats
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats_smoothed`: Smoothed seat demands
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_target_seats`: Seat allocation targets
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_seat_fair_frac`: Fair fraction of server's concurrency to allocate to each priority level that can use it
  - `apiserver_flowcontrol_current_limit_seats`: current derived number of execution seats available to each priority level
The possibility of borrowing means that the old metric `apiserver_flowcontrol_request_concurrency_limit` can no longer mean both the configured concurrency limit and the enforced concurrency limit. Henceforth it means the configured concurrency limit.'
apiChange.author: MikeSpreitzer
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Priority and Fairness has introduced a new feature called _borrowing_ that allows an API priority level
to borrow a number of seats from other priority level(s). As a cluster operator, you can enable borrowing
for a certain priority level configuration object via the two newly introduced fields `lendablePercent`, and
`borrowingLimitPercent` located under the `.spec.limited` field of the designated priority level.
This PR adds the following metrics.
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_nominal_limit_seats`: Nominal number of execution seats configured for each priority level
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_lower_limit_seats`: Configured lower bound on number of execution seats available to each priority level
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_upper_limit_seats`: Configured upper bound on number of execution seats available to each priority level
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats`: Observations, at the end of every nanosecond, of (the number of seats each priority level could use) / (nominal number of seats for that level)
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats_high_watermark`: High watermark, over last adjustment period, of demand_seats
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats_average`: Time-weighted average, over last adjustment period, of demand_seats
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats_stdev`: Time-weighted standard deviation, over last adjustment period, of demand_seats
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_demand_seats_smoothed`: Smoothed seat demands
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_target_seats`: Seat allocation targets
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_seat_fair_frac`: Fair fraction of server's concurrency to allocate to each priority level that can use it
- `apiserver_flowcontrol_current_limit_seats`: current derived number of execution seats available to each priority level

The possibility of borrowing means that the old metric apiserver_flowcontrol_request_concurrency_limit can no longer mean both the configured concurrency limit and the enforced concurrency limit.  Henceforth it means the configured concurrency limit.

enrichment.problem: The existing metric `apiserver_flowcontrol_request_concurrency_limit` was ambiguous, representing both the configured concurrency limit and the enforced limit for API priority levels. Operators and monitoring tools could not reliably distinguish the intended value. Additionally, there was no way to configure borrowing of seats between priority levels.
enrichment.affected: Operators using Priority and Fairness for API request throttling and any monitoring systems that relied on the old `apiserver_flowcontrol_request_concurrency_limit` metric.
enrichment.fix: Introduced borrowing support for API priority levels by adding `lendablePercent` and `borrowingLimitPercent` fields under `.spec.limited`. Added a suite of new metrics (e.g., `apiserver_flowcontrol_nominal_limit_seats`, `apiserver_flowcontrol_current_limit_seats`, demand and target seat metrics) to expose configured limits, actual allocations, and demand. Clarified that the legacy metric now only reports the configured concurrency limit.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now configure flexible seat borrowing to improve API request handling under load, and have richer observability into flow‑control behavior. Monitoring dashboards must be updated to interpret the renamed meaning of the old metric and to incorporate the new metrics for accurate capacity planning and troubleshooting.

apiChange.description: Graduated `ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy` feature to GA.
apiChange.author: avoltz
apiChange.userFacingChange: Graduate ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy feature to GA

enrichment.problem: The ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy field was in beta, requiring a feature gate and lacking a stable API, which prevented production use and caused uncertainty for users needing internal traffic routing control.
enrichment.affected: Users who configure or depend on ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy (previously in beta) and any workloads that rely on Service internal traffic routing.
enrichment.fix: Graduates ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy to GA, removing the feature gate, making the field stable in the core Service API, and providing default behavior and documentation for production workloads.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now rely on a stable internal traffic policy for Services without extra feature‑gate configuration, enabling predictable pod‑to‑pod communication within a Service and simplifying production deployments.

apiChange.description: '`NodeInclusionPolicy` in `podTopologySpread` plugin is now enabled by default.'
apiChange.author: kerthcet
apiChange.userFacingChange: NodeInclusionPolicy in podTopologySpread plugin is enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: The podTopologySpread scheduler plugin required an explicit NodeInclusionPolicy configuration, and the policy was disabled by default, forcing users to manually enable it to get node‑aware spreading behavior.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads that use podTopologySpread constraints (pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, etc.) because the scheduler now automatically applies the node inclusion policy.
enrichment.fix: NodeInclusionPolicy is now enabled by default in the podTopologySpread plugin, so the scheduler automatically applies node‑aware topology spreading without additional configuration.
enrichment.impact: Users of pod topology spread constraints get better default pod placement across nodes, simplifying configuration and improving workload distribution and resilience.

apiChange.description:
'Graduated `JobTrackingWithFinalizers` to stable.
Jobs created before the feature was enabled are still tracked without finalizers.
Jobs tracked with finalizers have the annotation batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking.
If the annotation is present and the user attempts to remove it, the control plane adds it back.
The annotation `batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking` is now deprecated.
The control plane will ignore it and stop adding it for new Jobs in v1.27.'
apiChange.author: alculquicondor
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Graduate JobTrackingWithFinalizers to stable.
Jobs created before the feature was enabled are still tracked without finalizers. Jobs tracked with finalizers have the annotation batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking.
If the annotation is present and the user attempts to remove it, the control plane adds it back.
The annotation batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking is deprecated. The control plane will ignore it and stop adding it for new Jobs in v1.27.

enrichment.problem: Job objects were tracked using a deprecated annotation (batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking) and without finalizers, which could lead to unreliable cleanup and lingering Pods. Users could also remove the annotation, causing the control plane to re‑add it inconsistently.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster using Job resources, especially those that relied on the batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking annotation or experienced lingering Pods after Job completion.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the JobTrackingWithFinalizers feature to GA. Jobs are now tracked via a controller‑added finalizer and receive the batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking annotation only for backward compatibility. The control plane enforces the finalizer, restores the annotation if manually removed, and deprecates the annotation for new Jobs (no longer added after v1.27).
enrichment.impact: Provides a reliable, stable mechanism for Job lifecycle tracking, reducing leftover Pods and eliminating reliance on a deprecated annotation. Users upgrading to v1.27 will see the annotation ignored, preventing unexpected behavior.

other.description: Dropped support for the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) version `v1alpha2`, which means that container runtimes just have to implement `v1`.
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: The kubelet no longer supports the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) version v1alpha2, so runtimes that only implement v1alpha2 cannot be used.
enrichment.affected: Users running container runtimes that only support CRI v1alpha2, affecting pod startup on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: Support for CRI v1alpha2 has been removed; runtimes must implement the stable CRI v1 version to be compatible with the kubelet.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using a container runtime that only implements CRI v1alpha2 will fail to start pods until the runtime is upgraded to support CRI v1, requiring administrators to update or replace the runtime.

other.description:
Added categories column to the `kubectl api-resources` command's wide output (`-o wide`).
Added `--categories` flag to the `kubectl api-resources` command, which can be used to filter the output to show only resources belonging to one or more categories.
other.author: brianpursley
other.userFacingChange:
Added categories column to the `kubectl api-resources` command's wide output (`-o wide`).
Added `--categories` flag to the `kubectl api-resources` command, which can be used to filter the output to show only resources belonging to one or more categories.

enrichment.problem: kubectl api-resources did not show the resource categories and lacked a way to filter resources by category, making it harder for users to discover and list related resources.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users who list API resources, especially when they need to discover or filter resources by logical categories.
enrichment.fix: Added a categories column to the wide output (-o wide) of kubectl api-resources and introduced a new --categories flag that filters the listed resources to those belonging to one or more specified categories.
enrichment.impact: Improves the usability of kubectl for operators and developers by allowing easier discovery of related resources and enabling scripts to target specific categories, reducing manual lookup effort.

other.description: release-note
other.author: yangjunmyfm192085

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Not specified
enrichment.fix: Not specified
enrichment.impact: Not specified

other.description: Scheduler dumper now exposes a summary to indicate the number of pending pods in each internal queue.
other.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: The scheduler dumper did not provide any visibility into how many pending pods were in each of its internal scheduling queues, making it difficult for operators to diagnose scheduling delays or bottlenecks.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and developers who rely on scheduler diagnostics to understand pod scheduling backlogs.
enrichment.fix: The kube-scheduler dumper now includes a summary section that reports the count of pending pods for each internal queue, exposing this information via the scheduler's diagnostic endpoints.
enrichment.impact: Operators gain better observability into the scheduler's internal state, enabling quicker identification of scheduling pressure points and more efficient troubleshooting of pod placement issues.

other.description: Deprecated beta APIs scheduled for removal in `v1.26` are no longer served. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-26 for more information.
other.author: liggitt
other.userFacingChange: ACTION REQUIRED: Deprecated beta APIs scheduled for removal in 1.26 are no longer served. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/#v1-26 for more information.

enrichment.problem: Beta APIs that were scheduled for removal in Kubernetes v1.26 are no longer served by the API server, causing any client that still uses those removed beta versions to receive errors.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads, controllers, scripts, or tools that still rely on the beta API versions scheduled for removal in v1.26.
enrichment.fix: The API server now stops serving the deprecated beta API groups/versions that were slated for removal, enforcing migration to the corresponding stable (GA) APIs.
enrichment.impact: Clusters will reject requests to the removed beta APIs, which can break applications, controllers, or scripts that have not been updated. Users must update manifests, clients, or controllers to use the supported GA APIs to keep the workloads functional.

other.description: e2e: tests can now register callbacks with `ginkgo.BeforeEach`, `ginkgo.AfterEach` or `ginkgo.DeferCleanup` directly after creating a framework instance and are guaranteed that their code is called after the framework is initialized and before it gets cleaned up. `ginkgo.DeferCleanup` replaces `f.AddAfterEach` and `AddCleanupAction` which got removed to simplify the framework.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: e2e: tests can now register callbacks with ginkgo.BeforeEach/AfterEach/DeferCleanup directly after creating a framework instance and are guaranteed that their code is called after the framework is initialized and before it gets cleaned up. ginkgo.DeferCleanup replaces f.AddAfterEach and AddCleanupAction which got removed to simplify the framework.

enrichment.problem: e2e test suites could not reliably register cleanup or setup callbacks after creating a test framework instance, and had to use the now-removed f.AddAfterEach and AddCleanupAction APIs, leading to ordering uncertainties and extra maintenance.
enrichment.affected: Developers writing Kubernetes e2e tests; any CI pipelines that rely on the e2e testing framework.
enrichment.fix: The framework now allows registration of callbacks directly with ginkgo.BeforeEach, ginkgo.AfterEach, and ginkgo.DeferCleanup immediately after framework creation. The callbacks are guaranteed to run after the framework is initialized and before it is torn down. The old f.AddAfterEach and AddCleanupAction functions have been removed in favor of ginkgo.DeferCleanup.
enrichment.impact: Test authors get a simpler, more predictable way to add per‑test setup and teardown logic, reducing test flakiness and maintenance overhead. The change does not affect cluster runtime behavior.

other.description: kubeadm: removed the usage of the `--container-runtime=remote` flag for the kubelet during kubeadm init/join/upgrade. The flag value `remote` had been the only possible value since `dockershim` was removed from the kubelet.
other.author: pacoxu
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: remove the usage of the --container-runtime=remote flag for the kubelet during kubeadm init/join/upgrade. The flag value "remote" has been the only possible value since dockershim was removed from the kubelet.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm passed the flag --container-runtime=remote to the kubelet during init/join/upgrade even though dockershim was removed and "remote" is the only valid value, making the flag redundant and potentially confusing.
enrichment.affected: Clusters provisioned or upgraded with kubeadm. Any node where kubeadm invokes the kubelet during init, join, or upgrade.
enrichment.fix: Removed the usage of the --container-runtime=remote flag from all kubeadm commands (init, join, upgrade). kubeadm now starts the kubelet without specifying this flag.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unnecessary flag warnings, reduces configuration noise, and aligns kubeadm with the current kubelet behavior where the container runtime flag is implicit. No functional change to clusters, but simplifies upgrade paths and documentation.

other.description: kubeadm: removed the toleration for the `node-role.kubernetes.io/master` taint from the CoreDNS deployment of `kubeadm`. With the 1.25 release of kubeadm the taint `node-role.kubernetes.io/master` is no longer applied to control plane nodes and the toleration for it can be removed with the release of 1.26. You can also perform the same toleration removal from your own addon manifests.
other.author: pacoxu
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: remove the toleration for the "node-role.kubernetes.io/master" taint from the CoreDNS deployment of kubeadm. With the 1.25 release of kubeadm the taint "node-role.kubernetes.io/master" is no longer applied to control plane nodes and the toleration for it can be removed with the release of 1.26. You can also perform the same toleration removal from your own addon manifests.

enrichment.problem: CoreDNS pods created by kubeadm include a toleration for the "node-role.kubernetes.io/master" taint even though, starting with kubeadm v1.25, control‑plane nodes no longer receive that taint. The unnecessary toleration adds noise to manifests and may cause confusion for users customizing addon deployments.
enrichment.affected: Clusters provisioned with kubeadm that use the default CoreDNS addon, and any users who have copied the CoreDNS manifest into their own addon manifests.
enrichment.fix: The CoreDNS deployment generated by kubeadm now omits the toleration for the "node-role.kubernetes.io/master" taint. Users can also manually remove this toleration from any custom addon manifests they manage.
enrichment.impact: Manifests become cleaner and easier to understand. There is no functional change to CoreDNS scheduling, but removing the stale toleration avoids potential misunderstanding and aligns manifests with the current taint behavior on control‑plane nodes.

other.description: `GlusterFS` in-tree storage driver which was deprecated in kubernetes 1.25 release is now removed entirely in 1.26.
other.author: humblec
other.userFacingChange: GlusterFS in-tree storage driver which was deprecated at kubernetes 1.25 release has been removed entirely in 1.26.

enrichment.problem: The in-tree GlusterFS storage driver, which had been deprecated in v1.25, has been removed in v1.26. Clusters that still rely on the in-tree driver will fail to attach or provision volumes after upgrading.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgrading to Kubernetes v1.26 that still have GlusterFS in-tree volume plugins enabled or existing PVs/PVCs that reference the in-tree driver.
enrichment.fix: The driver code has been deleted from the core Kubernetes codebase. Users must migrate to the external GlusterFS CSI driver (or another compatible storage solution) before upgrading to v1.26.
enrichment.impact: Without migration, workloads that use GlusterFS PersistentVolumes or StorageClasses will experience volume provisioning/attachment failures, leading to pod startup failures. Migration to CSI restores storage functionality.

other.description: Refactored `test/e2e/framework` so that the core framework is smaller. Optional functionality like resource monitoring, log size monitoring, metrics gathering and debug information dumping must be imported by specific e2e test suites. Init packages are provided which can be imported to re-enable the functionality that traditionally was in the core framework. If you have code that no longer compiles because of this PR, you can use the script [from a commit message](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/112043/commits/dfdf88d4faafa6fd39988832ea0ef6d668f490e9) to update that code.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: The test/e2e/framework was refactored so that the core framework is smaller. Optional functionality like resource monitoring, log size monitoring, metrics gathering and debug information dumping must be imported by specific e2e test suites. Init packages are provided which can be imported to re-enable the functionality that traditionally was in the core framework. If you have code that no longer compiles because of this PR, you can use the script [from a commit message](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/112043/commits/dfdf88d4faafa6fd39988832ea0ef6d668f490e9) to update that code.

enrichment.problem: The core e2e test framework was monolithic, and optional features like resource monitoring and metrics were always compiled in, causing larger binary size and compilation issues for test suites that only needed core functionality.
enrichment.affected: Developers of e2e test suites and CI pipelines that compile the Kubernetes test framework.
enrichment.fix: Refactored test/e2e/framework to keep only essential core code. Optional capabilities (resource monitoring, log size monitoring, metrics gathering, debug dumps) are now provided as separate init packages that test suites can import explicitly. A migration script is supplied to update existing code that relied on the previous unified imports.
enrichment.impact: Reduces e2e test binary size and compile time, and makes the framework more modular. Developers with existing e2e tests may need to adjust imports, but a provided script can automatically fix most compile errors.

other.description: Updated `cri-tools` to [v1.25.0(https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cri-tools/releases/tag/v1.25.0)
other.author: saschagrunert
other.userFacingChange: Updated cri-tools to [v1.25.0](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cri-tools/releases/tag/v1.25.0)

enrichment.problem: The cluster's bundled cri-tools version was outdated, missing recent bug fixes, compatibility improvements, and new features needed for up‑to‑date CRI debugging.
enrichment.affected: Users who run `crictl` or rely on cri-tools for debugging containers; any workflow that uses CRI tooling in CI/CD or troubleshooting.
enrichment.fix: Update the bundled cri-tools package to v1.25.0, bringing in the latest upstream changes.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators and developers get an up‑to‑date `crictl` CLI with improved stability, bug fixes, and support for newer container runtimes, reducing troubleshooting friction.

other.description: Moved `LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring` back to Alpha.
other.author: rphillips
other.userFacingChange: Fix a 1.25 regression updating mounted configmaps when the LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring feature is enabled. LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring feature gate is demoted back to Alpha.

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.25, when the LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring feature gate was enabled, updates to mounted ConfigMaps were not propagated to running pods, causing pods to see stale configuration data.
enrichment.affected: Users running Kubernetes 1.25 with LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring enabled, especially workloads that rely on dynamically updated ConfigMaps.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed and the feature gate was moved back to Alpha status, restoring correct ConfigMap update behavior when the feature is enabled.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that had the feature enabled now receive fresh ConfigMap data without needing to restart pods, preventing configuration drift and potential application errors.

other.description: Legacy klog flags are no longer available. Only `-v` and `-vmodule` are still supported.
other.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: Legacy klog command‑line flags (e.g., --logtostderr, --stderrthreshold, --vmodule, etc.) were removed from Kubernetes binaries, leaving only -v and -vmodule supported. Scripts, tooling, or operators that relied on those flags now see unknown‑flag errors and lack expected logging behavior.
enrichment.affected: Any deployment that starts Kubernetes components (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller‑manager, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) with legacy klog flags. Affects operators, CI/CD pipelines, and testing frameworks that embed those flags.
enrichment.fix: The binaries have been updated to drop all deprecated klog flags. Users must modify their startup commands or scripts to use only -v and -vmodule (or configure logging via environment variables) to control log verbosity.
enrichment.impact: Ensures a consistent, minimal logging flag set across the project and reduces maintenance burden. However, existing automation that passes removed flags will fail, requiring a quick update to avoid startup failures.

In 'kube-proxy`: The "userspace" proxy mode (deprecated for over a year) is no
longer supported on either Linux or Windows. Users should use "iptables" or "ipvs"
on Linux, or "kernelspace" on Windows.
other.author: knabben
other.userFacingChange: kube-proxy: The `userspace` proxy mode (deprecated for over a year) is no longer supported on either Linux or Windows.  Users should use `iptables` or `ipvs` on Linux, or `kernelspace` on Windows.

issueContext.title: Removing UserSpace Proxying from Kubernetes core/
issueContext.body:
#### What would you like to be added:

Today in sig-network we all totally decided  to remove the userspace linux and windows proxies from kubernetes core, consensus was reached amongst the few remaining users of the kube proxy in userspace (project antrea @antoninbas , as well as openshift engineers @danwinship).

Im not sure this requires a KEP since, after all, the userspace proxy is essentially basically an untested easter egg that resides in K8s for legacy purposes, but we can write one if folks really want one. 

My proposal would be:

1) Heavily comment the code that the proxy is being removed in 1.23, including deprecation on the flag options for the kube-proxy mode.

2) In 1.24, stop accepting any feature updates related to Kube proxy in userspace other then CVEs or compilation errors.

3) In 1.25, delete the existing Kubernetes code for userspace proxy.  During this time, we can integrate the code into https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kpng as a optional backend, which will give users the ability to play with a userspace proxy in a sandbox if they want to, while also allowing a 'non production' version of the userspace proxy to live on in an experimental state.  

Does anyone want to help or take this issue over? I have no strong opinions on the implementation :), but i think this is the fastest and easiest.  

#### Why is this needed:

At this point we are heavily lacking test coverage for the userspace proxy.
- It hasnt been updated to support endpoint slices
- topology features are also not supported
- we have other efforts in place to modularize kube-proxy some day anyways, and so removing what is in-tree is synergistic with those efforts
- on kind we know there will not be support for the userspace linux proxy  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind/pull/2264

enrichment.problem: The deprecated `userspace` proxy mode was still available in Kubernetes, but as of this release it is no longer supported on Linux or Windows, causing kube-proxy to fail to start for clusters that still rely on that mode.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster that configured kube-proxy with `--proxy-mode=userspace` on Linux or Windows will be affected; workloads relying on that mode will see network failures.
enrichment.fix: Support for `userspace` mode has been removed. Users must configure kube-proxy to use `iptables` or `ipvs` on Linux, or `kernelspace` on Windows.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that were using the userspace proxy will lose pod network connectivity until they switch to a supported mode. The change finalizes a year‑long deprecation, simplifying the code base and reducing unmaintained traffic‑distribution code.

issueContext.title: kubectl run accidentally exposes --kustomize flag
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The `kubectl run` command provides a `--kustomize` flag but this doesn't do anything.

```
❯ kubectl run --help | grep kustomize
  -k, --kustomize='': Process a kustomization directory. This flag can't be used together with -f or -R.
```

### What did you expect to happen?

most likely the flag shouldn't exist. I have no idea how kustomize could be useful here to start a single pod.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This creates a pod, and shows that `--kustomize NOTEXiSTING` is ignored:

```
kubectl -v=5  run --rm --attach --image=busybox testpod  --restart=Never --kustomize NOTEXiSTING -- /bin/sh -c 'echo STARTED'
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
❯ kubectl version --client
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"23", GitVersion:"v1.23.4", GitCommit:"e6c093d87ea4cbb530a7b2ae91e54c0842d8308a", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-02-16T12:30:48Z", GoVersion:"go1.17.6", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>Azure, K3OS</details>


### OS version

<details>
OSX 11.6.1 (Big Sur)
</details>


### Install tools

_No response_

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

_No response_

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

_No response_

issueContext.title: Remove the "CSRDuration" feature gate in Kube v1.26
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Remove the "CSRDuration" feature gate starting in Kube v1.26.

### Why is this needed?

PR #108782 proposes that the CertificateSigningRequest's Spec.ExpirationSeconds field be promoted to GA in v1.24. It was originally introduced as beta in v1.22 with a corresponding feature gate called "CSRDuration" to optionally disable it (see PR #99494).

If PR #108782 is merged and included in v1.24, then in v1.26 the "CSRDuration" feature gate should be removed.

See also https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108782#discussion_r830327266 where a member of SIG-auth asked me to create this issue.

enrichment.fix: The CSRDuration feature gate has been removed entirely from the source, eliminating the obsolete flag and related gating logic.
enrichment.impact: Upgrading to v1.26 no longer requires handling the CSRDuration flag; clusters are simpler and there is no functional change for users. Any existing configuration that referenced the flag will be ignored or cause a warning.

other.description: Renamed the feature gate for CEL in Admission Control to `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`.
other.author: cici37
other.userFacingChange: Rename the feature gate for CEL in Admission Control to `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`.

enrichment.problem: The feature gate controlling the use of CEL (Common Expression Language) in admission control was named ambiguously, and existing clusters that enabled the gate with the old name may encounter unexpected behavior or warnings after the rename.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where the CEL admission control feature gate is enabled via the API server command line. Administrators need to change `--feature-gates=CELAdmission=true` (or similar) to `--feature-gates=ValidatingAdmissionPolicy=true`.
enrichment.fix: Rename the feature gate to `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`, providing a clearer name that aligns with the feature's purpose. Clusters using the old gate name must update their `--feature-gates` flag to the new name.
enrichment.impact: Users who have manually enabled the CEL admission control feature gate must update their API server startup flags. No functional change to the admission control logic itself; the rename improves discoverability and reduces configuration errors.

other.description:
'`kubelet_kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_duration` was renamed to `kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_duration`
and `kubelet_kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_errors` was renamed to `kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_errors`.'
other.author: logicalhan
other.userFacingChange: `kubelet_kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_duration` is renamed `kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_duration` and `kubelet_kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_errors` is renamed `kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_errors`.

enrichment.problem: The kubelet metrics tracking the credential provider plugin duration and error count were named `kubelet_kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_duration` and `kubelet_kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_errors`. The duplicated "kubelet" prefix caused inconsistent naming and could break monitoring dashboards or alerts that reference the old metric names.
enrichment.affected: Users who instrumented, scraped, or created alerts on the `kubelet_kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_*` metrics (typically monitoring solutions like Prometheus, Grafana, or custom dashboards).
enrichment.fix: The metrics have been renamed to `kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_duration` and `kubelet_credential_provider_plugin_errors`, removing the redundant prefix and aligning with the naming convention used for other kubelet metrics.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring systems, alerting rules, and Grafana dashboards that reference the old metric names must be updated to the new names. After the change, metrics will be emitted under the new names, ensuring continued observability of the credential provider plugin behavior.

other.description: The in-tree cloud provider for OpenStack (and the cinder volume provider) has been removed. Please use the external cloud provider and csi driver from [cloud-provider-openstack](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-openstack) instead.
other.author: dims
other.userFacingChange: The in-tree cloud provider for OpenStack (and the cinder volume provider) has now been removed. Please use the external cloud provider and csi driver from https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-openstack instead.

enrichment.problem: The in-tree OpenStack cloud provider and the in-tree Cinder volume driver have been removed from Kubernetes, causing clusters that rely on these built‑in providers to fail to provision cloud resources or attach storage.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that were using the in‑tree OpenStack cloud provider or the in‑tree Cinder volume provider.
enrichment.fix: Users must migrate to the external OpenStack cloud provider and the OpenStack CSI driver available at https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-openstack.
enrichment.impact: Clusters configured with the deprecated in-tree OpenStack or Cinder providers will experience errors and must be updated to the external provider and CSI driver to continue using OpenStack cloud features and volume provisioning.

documentation.description: Clarified the default CFS quota period as being 100µs and not 100ms.
documentation.author: paskal

deprecation.description: kube-apiserver: the unused `--master-service-namespace` flag was deprecated and will be removed in v1.27.
deprecation.author: SataQiu
deprecation.userFacingChange: kube-apiserver: the unused '--master-service-namespace' flag is deprecated and will be removed in v1.27.

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver binary still accepted the '--master-service-namespace' flag, but the flag was never used and has no effect.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where administrators have configured the '--master-service-namespace' flag on the kube-apiserver.
enrichment.fix: The flag is now deprecated and will be removed in v1.27, so it can no longer be set.
enrichment.impact: Administrators who currently set or plan to set '--master-service-namespace' will see the flag rejected in v1.27, preventing reliance on a non‑functional option. No functional change to the cluster behavior.

apiChange.description: The list-type of the alpha resourceClaims field introduced to Pods in 1.26.0 was modified from "set" to "map", resolving an incompatibility with use of this schema in CustomResourceDefinitions and with server-side apply.
apiChange.author: JoelSpeed

enrichment.problem: The alpha `resourceClaims` field in Pods was defined as a list of type "set". This schema conflicted with how CustomResourceDefinitions and server-side apply handle list fields, causing compatibility errors when users tried to use `resourceClaims` via CRDs or SSA.
enrichment.affected: Users leveraging the alpha `resourceClaims` field in Pod specifications, especially those using CustomResourceDefinitions or server-side apply to manage Pods.
enrichment.fix: The list type for `resourceClaims` was changed from "set" to "map", aligning it with the expected schema used by CRDs and server-side apply, eliminating the incompatibility.
enrichment.impact: Users can now define and apply the `resourceClaims` field in Pods through CRDs and server-side apply without schema validation failures, restoring expected functionality for workloads that rely on this alpha feature.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.5
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version; the release updates the build process to use Go 1.19.5.
enrichment.affected: Developers who compile Kubernetes from source and users of the released binaries. All component binaries are rebuilt with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.19.5, incorporating the language's security patches, performance improvements, and new compiler features.
enrichment.impact: Provides up‑to‑date security and performance benefits for the Kubernetes binaries and ensures future compatibility with Go ecosystem. No functional changes for clusters, but source‑build users need Go 1.19.5 installed.

failingTest.description: Deflake a preemption test that may patch Nodes incorrectly.
failingTest.author: Huang-Wei

bugOrRegression.description: Client-go: fixes potential data races retrying requests using a custom io.Reader body; with this fix, only requests with no body or with string / []byte / runtime.Object bodies can be retried
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: client-go could encounter data races when retrying HTTP requests that use a custom io.Reader as the request body, leading to undefined behavior or crashes.
enrichment.affected: Applications and controllers using client-go that retry requests with custom io.Reader bodies could be affected by race conditions.
enrichment.fix: The retry logic was updated to only allow retries for requests with no body or bodies of type string, []byte, or runtime.Object, eliminating the unsafe use of custom io.Reader bodies.
enrichment.impact: Improves stability and correctness of client-go request retries, preventing race conditions for controllers and operators that rely on the library.

bugOrRegression.description: Do not include preemptor pod metadata in the event message
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: Event messages for preemption included the full metadata of the preemptor pod, causing noisy output and exposing unnecessary pod details.
enrichment.affected: Users and tooling that consume Kubernetes events, especially when monitoring preemption events, will see reduced payloads.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now omits preemptor pod metadata when constructing preemption event messages, keeping only essential information.
enrichment.impact: Events become smaller and clearer, reducing log clutter and avoiding inadvertent exposure of pod details, which improves observability and security.

bugOrRegression.description: Do not include preemptor pod metadata in the message of DisruptionTarget condition
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The DisruptionTarget condition message for preempted pods included metadata from the preemptor pod, leading to overly verbose or potentially sensitive information being exposed in pod status.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use pod preemption; pods that are preempted may have previously shown unnecessary preemptor metadata in their status conditions.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler was updated to omit any preemptor pod metadata from the DisruptionTarget condition message, leaving only the essential disruption information.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators and users see cleaner, more concise condition messages for preempted pods, reducing noise and avoiding accidental exposure of pod metadata.

bugOrRegression.description: Failed pods associated with a job with `parallelism = 1` are recreated by the job controller honoring exponential backoff delay again. However, for jobs with `parallelism > 1`, pods might be created without exponential backoff delay.
bugOrRegression.author: nikhita

enrichment.problem: When a Job has parallelism > 1, the job controller recreates failed pods without applying the exponential backoff delay, leading to rapid pod restarts after failures.
enrichment.affected: Users running Jobs with parallelism greater than one that experience pod failures. The rapid pod recreation could overwhelm the cluster or violate expected backoff semantics.
enrichment.fix: The job controller now applies the exponential backoff policy for pod recreation regardless of the Job's parallelism setting, ensuring the configured backoff delay is honored for all failed pods.
enrichment.impact: Prevents a surge of pod creations after failures, reducing unnecessary load on the cluster and preserving the intended backoff behavior for high‑parallelism jobs.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a regression that the scheduler always goes through all Filter plugins.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: A regression caused the kube-scheduler to invoke every Filter plugin for each pod, even when earlier plugins had already eliminated a node, leading to unnecessary processing and increased scheduling latency.
enrichment.affected: All clusters using the default kube-scheduler; workloads experience slower scheduling when many filter plugins are configured.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler’s filter loop was corrected to stop evaluating further Filter plugins once a node is filtered out, restoring the intended short‑circuit behavior.
enrichment.impact: Reduces CPU usage and latency during pod scheduling, especially in clusters with many filter plugins or large node pools, improving overall scheduling performance.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix bug in CRD Validation Rules (beta) and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (alpha) where all admission requests could result in `internal error: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3 evaluating rule: <rule name>` under certain circumstances.
bugOrRegression.author: jpbetz

enrichment.problem: A bug in the beta CRD Validation Rules and alpha ValidatingAdmissionPolicy caused a runtime panic (index out of range) during admission evaluation, leading to `internal error: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3 evaluating rule: <rule name>` for all admission requests under certain conditions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use beta CRD validation rules or alpha ValidatingAdmissionPolicy could experience failed admission requests, affecting any workload creation or update that triggers these validations.
enrichment.fix: Added proper bounds checking in the validation rule evaluation logic, preventing the out‑of‑range panic and ensuring admission requests are processed correctly.
enrichment.impact: Admission requests that previously failed with an internal error now succeed, restoring normal operation for clusters using CRD validation rules or ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and avoiding potential denial of resource creation or updates.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix clearing of rate-limiter for the queue of checks for cleaning stale pod disruption conditions. 
  The bug could result in the PDB synchronization updates firing too often or the pod disruption cleanups taking too long to happen.
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The rate‑limiter for the queue that checks and clears stale PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) conditions was not being reset properly. This caused either excessively frequent PDB synchronization updates or delayed cleanup of stale disruption conditions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using PodDisruptionBudgets; the PDB controller in kube‑controller‑manager could produce extra sync traffic or delayed cleanups.
enrichment.fix: Implemented proper clearing of the rate‑limiter when processing the stale‑condition queue, ensuring the timer is reset after each run.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unnecessary API server load from overly frequent PDB syncs and guarantees timely removal of stale pod‑disruption conditions, improving overall cluster stability and performance for workloads that rely on PDBs.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed DaemonSet to update the status even if it fails to create a pod.
bugOrRegression.author: gjkim42

enrichment.problem: The DaemonSet controller did not update the DaemonSet object's status when pod creation failed, leaving the status out‑of‑date and making it hard to detect rollout problems.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using DaemonSets could see misleading status when a pod failed to be created, affecting troubleshooting and automation that relies on accurate status.
enrichment.fix: The controller now writes status updates for a DaemonSet regardless of whether the pod creation succeeded, ensuring the status reflects both successes and failures.
enrichment.impact: Operators and higher‑level tools get accurate status information, improving observability and debugging of DaemonSet rollouts and preventing stale status from causing incorrect assumptions about pod health.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes stuck apiserver if an aggregated apiservice returned 304 Not Modified for aggregated discovery information
bugOrRegression.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver could become stuck when an aggregated APIService returned HTTP 304 Not Modified for discovery information, causing the API server to hang and become unresponsive.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use aggregated API services (e.g., custom APIs added via API aggregation) could experience a hung apiserver, affecting all kubectl and component interactions.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver now correctly handles 304 responses from aggregated API services during discovery, preventing the server from entering a deadlock state.
enrichment.impact: API server remains responsive even when aggregated services use 304 responses, ensuring continued cluster operation and avoiding outages for users of aggregated APIs.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixing issue in Winkernel Proxier - Unexpected active TCP connection drops while horizontally scaling the endpoints for a LoadBalancer Service with External Traffic Policy: Local
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: Active TCP connections were unexpectedly dropped when horizontally scaling the endpoints of a LoadBalancer Service that has externalTrafficPolicy set to Local, due to a bug in the Winkernel proxier implementation.
enrichment.affected: Users running LoadBalancer services with externalTrafficPolicy: Local, especially on Windows nodes where the Winkernel proxier is used, and who scale the service endpoints.
enrichment.fix: The Winkernel proxier was updated to correctly handle endpoint list changes without terminating existing connections, ensuring stable traffic during scaling operations.
enrichment.impact: LoadBalancer services with externalTrafficPolicy: Local now retain active connections during scaling, improving reliability and preventing service disruptions for workloads using this configuration.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixing issue with Winkernel Proxier - No ingress load balancer rules with endpoints to support load balancing when all the endpoints are terminating.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: The Windows kernel proxier (kube-proxy) failed to create ingress load balancer rules when all service endpoints were terminating, resulting in no load balancing rules being applied.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Windows nodes with the Winkernel proxier (kube-proxy) for Services/Ingress that have terminating endpoints.
enrichment.fix: The proxier logic was updated to always generate the necessary ingress load balancer rules even when all endpoints are in a terminating state, ensuring proper rule creation.
enrichment.impact: Windows clusters that rely on the Winkernel proxier for load-balanced services will now see correct traffic routing and avoid service interruptions caused by missing load balancer rules.

bugOrRegression.description: Optimizing loadbalancer creation with the help of attribute Internal Traffic Policy: Local
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: Creating LoadBalancer services with the InternalTrafficPolicy set to Local caused the controller to provision load balancers for all cluster nodes, leading to unnecessary resource allocation and slower service provisioning.
enrichment.affected: Users creating Service objects of type LoadBalancer with InternalTrafficPolicy set to Local; clusters using cloud provider load balancers.
enrichment.fix: The change adds logic that leverages the InternalTrafficPolicy: Local attribute during load balancer creation, ensuring that only nodes with local endpoints are considered, thus optimizing the provisioning process.
enrichment.impact: LoadBalancer services are created more quickly and with fewer cloud resources, reducing cost and improving overall networking performance for workloads that use internal traffic policy Local.

apiChange.description: A fix in the resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1/ResourceClaim API avoids harmless (?) ".status.reservedFor: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" errors in the apiserver. Validation now rejects the incorrect reuse of the same UID in different entries.
apiChange.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: The apiserver emitted confusing validation errors like ".status.reservedFor: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" when the same UID was reused in multiple entries of a ResourceClaim's status, even though the condition was harmless.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the v1alpha1 ResourceClaim API (e.g., workloads that allocate resources via CSI or other drivers) and any administrators monitoring apiserver logs.
enrichment.fix: Added stricter validation in the resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1 ResourceClaim API to reject duplicate UID reuse across status.reservedFor entries, eliminating the erroneous status map error.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer see noisy, misleading validation errors in apiserver logs, reducing operator confusion and ensuring clearer status handling for ResourceClaim objects.

apiChange.description: K8s.io/component-base/logs: usage of the pflag values in a normal Go flag set led to panics when printing the help message
apiChange.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: When the component-base/logs package used pflag values inside a regular Go flag set, printing the help message caused a panic, crashing the binary.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes binary that imports k8s.io/component-base/logs and uses a normal Go flag set (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl) would panic when printing help.
enrichment.fix: The code now correctly handles pflag values in a standard flag set, avoiding the panic when the help output is generated.
enrichment.impact: Commands that previously crashed when users invoked "-h/--help" now work correctly, restoring normal CLI usability and preventing unexpected process termination.

feature.description:
Kubelet TCP and HTTP probes are more effective using networking resources: conntrack entries, sockets, ... 
  This is achieved by reducing the TIME-WAIT state of the connection to 1 second, instead of the defaults 60 seconds. This allows kubelet to free the socket, and free conntrack entry and ephemeral port associated.
feature.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: Kubelet TCP and HTTP health probes linger in the TIME-WAIT state for 60 seconds, consuming sockets, conntrack entries, and ephemeral ports. On nodes with many probes this can exhaust these resources and cause probe failures.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet that perform TCP/HTTP probes, especially clusters with high probe frequency or many pods.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now sets the TIME-WAIT state for probe connections to 1 second, allowing the socket, conntrack entry, and port to be released promptly.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of health checks and prevents resource exhaustion on nodes, reducing false‑negative probe results and improving overall cluster stability.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes source was built with an older Go compiler, limiting use of newer language features, security patches, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: Anyone compiling Kubernetes from source, including developers, CI systems, and custom binary distributors.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile Kubernetes with Go 1.19.6.
enrichment.impact: Users building Kubernetes from source (including CI pipelines and custom binaries) can now benefit from the latest Go runtime improvements, security fixes, and better compatibility with newer Go ecosystem tools.

feature.description: Use HorizontalPodAutoscaler v2 for kubectl
feature.author: a7i

enrichment.problem: kubectl defaulted to the HorizontalPodAutoscaler v1 API, preventing users from creating or managing HPA objects with v2 features such as multiple or custom metrics.
enrichment.affected: Developers and operators who use kubectl to create or manage HorizontalPodAutoscaler resources, especially those needing v2 functionality.
enrichment.fix: kubectl now targets the HorizontalPodAutoscaler v2 API version, enabling full use of v2 capabilities when creating, updating, or describing HPA resources.
enrichment.impact: Users can leverage advanced autoscaling options (e.g., multiple metrics, external metrics) directly via kubectl without workarounds, simplifying deployment of modern HPA configurations.

bugOrRegression.description: Do not add DisruptionTarget condition by PodGC for pods which are in terminal phase
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The Pod Garbage Collector (PodGC) incorrectly added the DisruptionTarget condition to pods that had already reached a terminal phase (Succeeded or Failed), leading to inaccurate pod status information.
enrichment.affected: Pods that have completed (Succeeded/Failed) and any controllers or tools that rely on the DisruptionTarget condition for status decisions.
enrichment.fix: PodGC now checks the pod phase before adding the DisruptionTarget condition and skips this step for pods in a terminal phase.
enrichment.impact: Pods in terminal states no longer receive a misleading DisruptionTarget condition, improving status accuracy and preventing downstream components or users from treating completed pods as being in disruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Enforce nodeName cannot be set along with non-empty schedulingGates
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: Pods could be created with both spec.nodeName and a non‑empty spec.schedulingGates, which is contradictory and could cause the pod to remain unschedulable or behave unpredictably.
enrichment.affected: Any pod (including those managed by Deployments, StatefulSets, Jobs, etc.) that specifies both nodeName and one or more schedulingGates.
enrichment.fix: Added validation that rejects pod creation or update when nodeName is set together with any schedulingGates, ensuring the two fields are mutually exclusive.
enrichment.impact: Prevents pods from getting stuck in a pending state due to conflicting scheduling constraints, improving reliability for workloads that use explicit node assignment or scheduling gates.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug that caused to panic the apiserver when trying to allocate a Service with a dynamic ClusterIP and it has been configured with Service CIDRs with a /28 mask for IPv4 and a /124 mask for IPv6
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: The API server panics and crashes when a Service with a dynamically allocated ClusterIP is created while the Service CIDR is configured with an extremely small mask (/28 for IPv4 or /124 for IPv6).
enrichment.affected: Users creating Services with dynamic ClusterIPs on clusters that use a /28 IPv4 Service CIDR or a /124 IPv6 Service CIDR were unable to create services and risked a full API server outage.
enrichment.fix: Added validation and corrected handling of Service CIDR masks during dynamic ClusterIP allocation to prevent the panic path and allow Service creation with those CIDR sizes.
enrichment.impact: Prevents API server crashes that could make the entire cluster unavailable when users create Services with narrow CIDR ranges, restoring normal Service provisioning functionality.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix nil pointer error in nodevolumelimits csi logging
bugOrRegression.author: sunnylovestiramisu

enrichment.problem: The scheduler's nodevolumelimits plugin could panic with a nil pointer when attempting to log CSI volume information, leading to crashes during pod placement.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have the nodevolumelimits scheduling plugin enabled and use CSI drivers for volume provisioning.
enrichment.fix: Added a nil check before accessing CSI logging fields in the nodevolumelimits code, preventing the nil pointer dereference.
enrichment.impact: Prevents scheduler crashes, ensuring reliable pod scheduling for clusters that use CSI volume limits.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix the regression that introduced 34s timeout for DELETECOLLECTION calls
bugOrRegression.author: tkashem

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced a 34-second timeout for DELETECOLLECTION API calls, causing bulk delete operations to fail or be aborted before completion.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or tooling that performs DELETECOLLECTION requests against the Kubernetes API, such as kubectl bulk deletes, controllers, and automation scripts.
enrichment.fix: The timeout handling for DELETECOLLECTION requests was corrected, restoring the expected behavior and allowing the operation to complete without premature timeout.
enrichment.impact: Users and controllers that rely on bulk delete (e.g., `kubectl delete <resource> --all` or garbage‑collection) can now delete collections reliably, preventing partial deletions and reducing operational friction.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed bug which caused the status of Indexed Jobs to only be updated when there are newly completed indexes. The completed indexes are now updated if the .status.completedIndexes has values outside of the [0, .spec.completions> range
bugOrRegression.author: danielvegamyhre

enrichment.problem: The status of Indexed Jobs was only updated when new indexes completed. If .status.completedIndexes contained values outside the valid completions range, the job status remained stale and did not reflect those completed indexes.
enrichment.affected: Users running Indexed Jobs (Job resources with completionMode: Indexed) who rely on correct .status.completedIndexes reporting.
enrichment.fix: The job controller now updates the Job status whenever .status.completedIndexes has values outside the [0, .spec.completions) range, ensuring the status is always in sync with the actual completed indexes.
enrichment.impact: Users of Indexed Jobs get accurate status reporting, which improves observability and prevents confusion about job progress when out‑of‑range indexes are present.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes bug in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy alpha which prevented policies from using a paramKind previously used by another policy
bugOrRegression.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: When using the alpha ValidatingAdmissionPolicy feature, a policy could not reference a paramKind that was already used by another policy, causing the second policy to be rejected or ignored.
enrichment.affected: Users who defined more than one ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that referenced the same paramKind were unable to apply those policies.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the admission registration logic so that multiple ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects can share the same paramKind without conflict.
enrichment.impact: Allows developers to compose multiple validating admission policies that reuse a common parameter definition, improving modularity and preventing admission errors in clusters that use this alpha feature.

bugOrRegression.description: Golang.org/x/net updates to v0.7.0 to fix CVE-2022-41723
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes components were using golang.org/x/net version vulnerable to CVE-2022-41723, which could allow remote code execution or denial-of-service attacks in networking code.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries that vendor golang.org/x/net (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, and cloud-provider binaries) were potentially vulnerable.
enrichment.fix: The dependency has been upgraded to golang.org/x/net v0.7.0, which contains the patches that remediate CVE-2022-41723.
enrichment.impact: Remediates a security vulnerability in the networking library used by many Kubernetes components, reducing the risk of exploitation in production clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: The Kubernetes API server now correctly detects and closes existing TLS connections when its client certificate file for kubelet authentication has been rotated.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: After rotating the kubelet client certificate file, the API server kept existing TLS connections open, allowing kubelets to continue authenticating with the old (now revoked) certificate.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet nodes that authenticate to the API server with client certificates, especially clusters performing regular certificate rotation.
enrichment.fix: The API server now watches the client‑certificate file used for kubelet authentication and, when it changes, proactively closes any existing TLS connections so that a new handshake uses the refreshed certificate.
enrichment.impact: Rotated certificates take effect immediately, preventing nodes from using stale credentials, improving security and avoiding authentication failures that could disrupt node‑API communication.

apiChange.description: Volumes: `resource.claims` gets cleared for PVC specs during create or update of a pod spec with inline PVC template or of a PVC because it has no effect.
apiChange.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: The `resource.claims` field in PVC specifications was being persisted during pod creation or PVC updates even though it has no functional effect, leading to unnecessary data in the API objects.
enrichment.affected: Users who include `resource.claims` in inline PVC templates within pod specs or directly in PVC objects could see the field omitted after create/update operations.
enrichment.fix: The API server now clears the `resource.claims` field for PVC specs when creating or updating a pod that includes an inline PVC template, or when updating a PVC directly, ensuring the field is not stored.
enrichment.impact: Reduces clutter in object specifications, prevents user confusion about a non‑functional field, and aligns the API with actual behavior, improving consistency for users managing volumes and PVCs.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.7
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes source was built with an older Go version, which could lack recent security fixes, performance improvements, and compatibility with newer Go toolchains.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI pipelines that build Kubernetes from source; all Kubernetes components compiled with the new toolchain.
enrichment.fix: Update the build configuration to use Go 1.19.7, recompiling all Kubernetes components with this newer Go release.
enrichment.impact: Projects that compile Kubernetes from source will benefit from Go's security patches, bug fixes, and performance enhancements, reducing build‑time issues and ensuring future compatibility.

feature.description: The go version defined in `.go-version` is now fetched when invoking test, build, and code generation targets if the current go version does not match it. Set $FORCE_HOST_GO=y while testing or building to skip this behavior, or set $GO_VERSION to override the selected go version.
feature.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: When invoking test, build, or code generation make targets, the host Go version was used even if it differed from the version specified in the repository's .go-version file, leading to inconsistent builds and potential test failures.
enrichment.affected: Developers building or testing Kubernetes and CI systems that run make test/build/codegen targets.
enrichment.fix: The make targets now automatically fetch and use the Go version defined in .go-version when the current host Go version does not match. Users can skip this auto-selection with FORCE_HOST_GO=y or override the selected version via GO_VERSION.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines get reproducible builds and test runs, reducing build breakages caused by Go version mismatches.

failingTest.description: Fixed panic in vSphere e2e tests.
failingTest.author: jsafrane

bugOrRegression.description: Fix data race in kube-scheduler when preemption races with a Pod update.
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: A data race in kube-scheduler could occur when a preemption operation runs concurrently with an update to a Pod, leading to inconsistent scheduling state or missed preemption decisions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where preemption is enabled and Pods are frequently updated; any workloads that depend on preemption to free resources.
enrichment.fix: Added proper synchronization in the scheduler code to eliminate the race condition between preemption handling and Pod updates.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that preemption works reliably even when Pods are being updated, preventing unexpected scheduling behavior and improving cluster stability for workloads that rely on preemption.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix log line in scheduler that inaccurately implies that volume binding has finalized
bugOrRegression.author: TommyStarK

enrichment.problem: The scheduler logged a message that suggested volume binding had completed even when it had not, which could mislead operators.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and developers who rely on scheduler logs to understand volume binding status.
enrichment.fix: The log message has been corrected to accurately reflect that volume binding is still in progress or not yet finalized.
enrichment.impact: Prevents confusion during debugging and ensures logs correctly represent the state of volume binding.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix race in alpha aggregated discovery handler
  Yes, discovery document will correctly return the resources for aggregated apiservers that do not implement aggregated disovery
bugOrRegression.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: A race condition in the alpha aggregated discovery handler could cause the discovery document to omit resources from aggregated API servers that do not implement the aggregated discovery endpoint, leading to incomplete discovery information for clients.
enrichment.affected: Clients performing discovery against the API server and any workloads using aggregated API servers that do not implement aggregated discovery.
enrichment.fix: The race condition was fixed so that the discovery document reliably includes resources from all aggregated API servers, even when they lack an aggregated discovery implementation.
enrichment.impact: Clients and tools that rely on the discovery API (e.g., kubectl, client libraries) will now receive a complete list of resources, preventing errors and improving compatibility with aggregated API servers.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixed a bug where Kubernetes would apply a default StorageClass to a PersistentVolumeClaim,
  even when the deprecated annotation `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class` was set.
bugOrRegression.author: cvvz

enrichment.problem: When a PersistentVolumeClaim included the deprecated annotation `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class`, Kubernetes still applied the cluster's default StorageClass, ignoring the annotation.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that creates a PersistentVolumeClaim with the deprecated `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class` annotation expecting no default StorageClass to be applied.
enrichment.fix: The PVC controller now respects the deprecated storage‑class annotation and refrains from automatically attaching the default StorageClass when the annotation is present.
enrichment.impact: Users relying on the old annotation to prevent default storage provisioning (e.g., for manual volume binding or custom class selection) will now get the intended behavior, avoiding unexpected volume provisioning and potential data placement issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed an EndpointSlice Controller hashing bug that could cause EndpointSlices to incorrectly handle Pods with duplicate IP addresses. For example this could happen when a new Pod reused an IP that was also assigned to a Pod in a completed state.
bugOrRegression.author: qinqon

enrichment.problem: The EndpointSlice controller used a hashing algorithm that could mis-handle Pods that shared the same IP address. When a new Pod was assigned an IP that was still present on a completed (previous) Pod, the controller could generate incorrect EndpointSlices, leading to stale or wrong endpoint data for Services.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads that experience IP address reuse, such as high churn pod environments, clusters with limited IP ranges, or test clusters that rapidly create and delete Pods.
enrichment.fix: The hashing logic in the EndpointSlice controller was corrected to properly account for Pods with duplicate IPs, ensuring each EndpointSlice uniquely represents the current set of live Pods even when IP addresses are reused.
enrichment.impact: Services will now route traffic to the correct, currently running Pods even in environments where IP addresses are quickly recycled, preventing traffic loss or misrouting and improving reliability of workloads that rely on fast pod turnover.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed performance regression in scheduler caused by frequent metric lookup on critical code path.
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: Scheduler latency regressed because it performed frequent metric lookups on a critical code path, slowing down pod scheduling.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that rely on the default kube-scheduler experienced slower pod placement, especially under heavy load.
enrichment.fix: Modified the scheduler to reduce the frequency of metric lookups on the hot path, restoring its original performance characteristics.
enrichment.impact: Improves scheduler throughput and reduces scheduling delays, benefiting clusters with high scheduling volumes or large numbers of pods.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixing issue with Winkernel Proxier - ClusterIP Loadbalancers are missing if the ExternalTrafficPolicy is set to Local and the available endpoints are all remoteEndpoints.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: ClusterIP LoadBalancer objects were not created on Windows nodes when using the winkernel proxier if the Service’s externalTrafficPolicy was set to Local and all the Service’s endpoints were on remote nodes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Windows nodes with kube-proxy in winkernel mode; Services of type ClusterIP/LoadBalancer that have externalTrafficPolicy=Local and only remote endpoints.
enrichment.fix: The winkernel proxier logic was updated to correctly handle the case where all endpoints are remote, ensuring that a LoadBalancer is still allocated for Services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads that rely on Services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local now receive proper load‑balancing and traffic routing, preventing loss of connectivity and eliminating the need for work‑arounds such as changing the policy to Cluster.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixing issue with Winkernel Proxier - IPV6 load balancer policies are missing when service is configured with ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: When a Service is configured with `ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack`, the Winkernel (Windows) kube-proxy fails to generate IPv6 load balancer policies, causing IPv6 traffic to be dropped or not correctly load‑balanced.
enrichment.affected: Users with Services using `ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack` on Windows nodes (Winkernel proxier). IPv6 traffic to those Services was previously not load‑balanced.
enrichment.fix: The Winkernel proxier now correctly creates and applies IPv6 load balancer policies for Services that require dual‑stack IP families.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that run Windows nodes and use dual‑stack Services will see proper IPv6 load balancing again, restoring expected network connectivity for workloads that depend on IPv6.

bugOrRegression.description: Make kubectl diff --prune behave correctly with the --selector/-l flag
bugOrRegression.author: nathanmartins

enrichment.problem: `kubectl diff --prune` did not respect the `--selector` (or `-l`) flag, leading to incorrect pruning behavior and inaccurate diff output when users filtered resources by label.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes CLI users running `kubectl diff` with `--prune` and `--selector`/`-l`. The issue affected any workflow that used these flags together.
enrichment.fix: The diff command's implementation was updated so that the prune operation correctly applies the label selector, ensuring only the resources matching the selector are considered for pruning and diff comparison.
enrichment.impact: Users who rely on `kubectl diff` with `--prune` and label selectors now receive accurate diff results, preventing confusion and potential accidental deletions of unintended resources.

bugOrRegression.description: Remove check for CSI driver running on node for CSI migration
bugOrRegression.author: sunnylovestiramisu

enrichment.problem: Kubelet enforced a check that a CSI driver must be running on the node before allowing CSI migration, causing pods that relied on migrated in‑tree storage to fail to start when the driver was not present on every node.
enrichment.affected: Users migrating in‑tree storage plugins to CSI, especially those with CSI drivers deployed as DaemonSets or only on a subset of nodes.
enrichment.fix: The node‑level CSI driver presence check was removed, allowing CSI migration to proceed even if the driver is not running on a particular node.
enrichment.impact: Clusters performing CSI migration can now complete the migration without needing to pre‑install the driver on every node, preventing pod startup failures and simplifying upgrade paths for storage users.

bugOrRegression.description: Set device stage path whenever available for expansion during mount
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: During CSI volume expansion, the kubelet did not set the device stage path when it was available, causing expansion to fail or use incorrect mount paths.
enrichment.affected: Pods using CSI volumes that support online expansion, particularly those with drivers that provide a device stage path.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now sets the device stage path whenever it is present during the mount operation, ensuring proper handling of volume expansion.
enrichment.impact: Users who rely on CSI drivers with volume expansion will experience reliable expansions without mount errors, improving stability of stateful workloads.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.8
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version, lacking recent language/runtime fixes and improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters and users, since every component (apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) is now built with the newer Go compiler.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.19.8 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components benefit from the latest Go security patches, performance enhancements, and language features, improving overall binary reliability and reducing exposure to known Go-level issues.
