feature.description: Unlocked the `CSIMigrationvSphere` feature gate. The change allow users to continue using the in-tree vSphere driver,pending a vSphere CSI driver release that has with GA support for Windows, XFS, and raw block access.
feature.author: msau42

enrichment.problem: The CSIMigrationvSphere feature gate was locked, which could prevent clusters from continuing to use the in-tree vSphere storage driver after upgrades, especially for workloads requiring Windows, XFS, or raw block support that were not yet available in the GA vSphere CSI driver.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using the in-tree vSphere storage driver, particularly those with Windows workloads, XFS volumes, or raw block access, may be impacted by the gate being locked.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is unlocked, allowing clusters to keep using the in-tree vSphere driver until a vSphere CSI driver with GA support for Windows, XFS, and raw block is released.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on the legacy vSphere driver (including Windows pods, XFS filesystems, and raw block volumes) can upgrade without losing storage functionality, providing a smoother migration path to CSI.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix missing delete events on informer re-lists to ensure all delete events are correctly emitted and using the latest known object state, so that all event handlers and stores always reflect the actual apiserver state as best as possible
bugOrRegression.author: odinuge

enrichment.problem: Informer relists could miss delete events, causing handlers and stores to retain objects that were removed from the apiserver.
enrichment.affected: Controllers, custom controllers, operators, and any client-go users that rely on informers for watch semantics.
enrichment.fix: During informer relist, generate delete events for objects that disappear, using the latest known object state, ensuring all delete events are emitted.
enrichment.impact: Controllers and any code that relies on informers will see a consistent view of the cluster state, preventing stale data, leaks, or incorrect behavior.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: Route controller should update routes with NodeIP changed
bugOrRegression.author: lzhecheng

enrichment.problem: The cloud route controller did not modify existing cloud routes when a node's IP address changed, leaving stale routes that could cause traffic to be sent to the wrong destination.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the cloud-provider route controller (cloud-controller-manager) where nodes can change their IP address.
enrichment.fix: The controller now watches for NodeIP changes and updates the associated cloud routes so they always point to the node's current IP.
enrichment.impact: Ensures reliable network connectivity for workloads after node IP changes (e.g., node reboot or migration). Prevents traffic loss or misrouting in clusters that rely on cloud provider routes.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed two regressions introduced by the PodDisruptionConditions feature (on by default in 1.26):

enrichment.problem: Two regressions were introduced when the PodDisruptionConditions feature was enabled by default in v1.26, causing unexpected behavior in pod disruption handling (e.g., pods not reporting proper disruption conditions or PDBs not being respected).
enrichment.affected: All workloads that use PodDisruptionBudgets or depend on pod disruption conditions, such as Deployments, StatefulSets, and DaemonSets.
enrichment.fix: Both regressions have been fixed, restoring correct PodDisruptionConditions behavior and ensuring pod disruption budgets work as intended.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on PodDisruptionBudgets and the new disruption conditions will again see accurate pod status and reliable eviction handling, preventing unintended downtime or scheduling issues.

bugOrRegression.description: pod eviction API calls returned spurious precondition errors and required a second evict API call to succeed

enrichment.problem: Eviction API calls sometimes returned a precondition error even though the pod was eligible for eviction, causing the first request to fail and requiring a second retry to succeed.
enrichment.affected: Any component or user that invokes the pod eviction subresource, such as kube-controller-manager, deployment/replicaset controllers, and kubectl evict, experienced an extra failed request.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the apiserver eviction logic to correctly evaluate preconditions, eliminating the spurious precondition error so that a single eviction request succeeds when valid.
enrichment.impact: Clients (kubectl, controllers, scripts) no longer need to implement retry logic for evictions, reducing latency and preventing unnecessary error handling in workload controllers.

bugOrRegression.description: dry-run eviction API calls persisted a DisruptionTarget condition into the pod being evicted
bugOrRegression.author: atiratree

enrichment.problem: When eviction API calls were made with dry-run=true, the server incorrectly persisted a DisruptionTarget condition on the pod being evicted instead of treating the request as a no‑op.
enrichment.affected: Users who performed dry‑run eviction API calls; pods that were subject to those calls could end up with an erroneous DisruptionTarget condition.
enrichment.fix: The eviction endpoint now respects dry-run semantics and no longer writes the DisruptionTarget condition to the pod object during a dry‑run eviction request.
enrichment.impact: Pods are no longer incorrectly marked as DisruptionTarget after a dry‑run eviction, preventing false alerts or controller actions that rely on this condition.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes a regression in the pod binding subresource to honor the `metadata.uid` precondition.
  This allows kube-scheduler to ensure it is assigns node names to the same instances of pods it made scheduling decisions for.
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: A regression in the pod binding subresource caused the API server to ignore the `metadata.uid` precondition, so kube-scheduler could bind a node name to a different pod instance than the one it scheduled.
enrichment.affected: kube-scheduler and any pods being scheduled that rely on the binding subresource; clusters could see incorrect pod placement without this fix.
enrichment.fix: The pod binding subresource now correctly honors the `metadata.uid` precondition, ensuring that the node assignment is applied only to the exact pod instance the scheduler made its decision for.
enrichment.impact: Prevents mismatched pod bindings and potential scheduling anomalies, improving reliability of pod placement and avoiding situations where pods could be bound to the wrong instance.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: Fix fs quota monitoring on volumes
bugOrRegression.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: The kubelet did not correctly monitor filesystem quota usage on mounted volumes, so it could fail to detect when a volume exceeded its configured quota.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kubelet with volumes that have filesystem quotas enabled (e.g., CSI drivers that support quota).
enrichment.fix: The kubelet implementation was updated to properly track and evaluate filesystem quota metrics for each volume, ensuring quota breaches are detected and appropriate actions (e.g., eviction) are taken.
enrichment.impact: Users with volumes that enforce filesystem quotas now get reliable quota enforcement, preventing pods from over-consuming storage and avoiding node disk‑pressure issues.

apiChange.description: Added error handling for seccomp localhost configurations that do not properly set a localhostProfile
apiChange.author: cji

enrichment.problem: When a pod or node configuration used a seccomp localhost profile without specifying a valid localhostProfile, the kubelet did not handle the situation properly, leading to unclear errors or potential node instability.
enrichment.affected: Users who configure seccomp localhost profiles on pods or nodes, especially those with mis‑typed or missing localhostProfile paths, could experience node or pod failures.
enrichment.fix: Added validation and explicit error handling for seccomp localhost configurations that lack a proper localhostProfile, ensuring the kubelet returns a clear error instead of failing silently or crashing.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators configuring seccomp profiles now receive helpful error messages, preventing hidden failures and improving node reliability and security posture.

apiChange.description: Fixed an issue where kubelet does not set case-insensitive headers for http probes. (#117182, @dddddai)
apiChange.author: dddddai

enrichment.problem: Kubelet failed to set HTTP probe request headers case‑insensitively, causing probes that rely on specific header capitalization to be rejected or misinterpreted.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use HTTP liveness/readiness probes with custom headers on nodes running the affected kubelet version.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now normalises and sends HTTP probe headers in a case‑insensitive manner, ensuring they are accepted by servers regardless of header case.
enrichment.impact: Readiness and liveness HTTP probes work reliably for workloads that specify custom headers, preventing unnecessary pod restarts or traffic routing errors.

apiChange.description: Revised the comment about the feature-gate level for PodFailurePolicy from alpha to beta
apiChange.author: kerthcet

enrichment.problem: The code comment for the PodFailurePolicy feature gate incorrectly indicated it was at the alpha stage, which could mislead users about its maturity.
enrichment.affected: Developers and cluster operators who read the source or generated docs to determine the maturity of the PodFailurePolicy feature gate.
enrichment.fix: Updated the comment to state that the PodFailurePolicy feature gate is now at the beta stage.
enrichment.impact: Provides accurate documentation of the feature-gate level, helping users understand the stability of PodFailurePolicy and make informed decisions when enabling it.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.19.9
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version, which could miss upstream Go security fixes, bug fixes, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and users who run the official binaries are affected because the binaries they download are now compiled with Go 1.19.9.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile the entire Kubernetes codebase with Go 1.19.9, incorporating the latest Go runtime/security patches.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, etc.) are now built with a newer, more secure and performant Go toolchain, reducing potential vulnerabilities and benefiting from Go runtime improvements without requiring changes from users.

failingTest.description: Allow Azure Disk e2es to use newer topology labels if available from nodes
failingTest.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: Multiple security vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-27561, CVE-2023-25809, CVE-2023-28642) were present in runc v1.1.4, potentially allowing container breakouts or privilege escalation.
enrichment.affected: Any pod/container launched via the CRI that uses the vulnerable runc version, typically all workloads on nodes running kubelet with runc v1.1.4.
enrichment.fix: The bundled runc binary is upgraded from v1.1.4 to the patched v1.1.5 version, which incorporates fixes for the reported CVEs.
enrichment.impact: Clusters running workloads with the affected runc version are protected from the identified security issues, reducing the risk of container escape and preserving node and cluster integrity.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed cgroup removal error when using runc binary >= 1.1.6
bugOrRegression.author: dims

enrichment.problem: When the node uses runc version 1.1.6 or newer, the kubelet fails to remove the container's cgroup, resulting in cleanup errors and lingering cgroups.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet on nodes that use runc binary version 1.1.6 or newer.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now detects the newer runc behavior and adjusts its cgroup removal logic to succeed, eliminating the error.
enrichment.impact: Nodes running kubelet with runc >=1.1.6 no longer encounter cgroup cleanup failures, improving node stability and preventing resource leaks.

bugOrRegression.description: During device plugin allocation, resources requested by the pod can only be allocated if the device plugin has registered itself to kubelet AND healthy devices are present on the node to be allocated. If these conditions are not sattisfied, the pod would fail with `UnexpectedAdmissionError` error.
bugOrRegression.author: swatisehgal

enrichment.problem: Pods that request device plugin resources could fail during allocation with an UnexpectedAdmissionError when the device plugin was not registered with the kubelet or when no healthy devices were present on the node.
enrichment.affected: Pods that request device plugin resources on nodes where the plugin is unregistered or devices are unhealthy were experiencing admission failures.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now checks that the device plugin is registered and that healthy devices exist before attempting allocation. If the conditions are not met, the allocation is rejected with a proper error instead of triggering an UnexpectedAdmissionError.
enrichment.impact: Prevents pod admission failures for workloads relying on device plugins, improving reliability of GPU, FPGA, and other hardware accelerator workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix incorrect calculation for ResourceQuota with PriorityClass as its scope.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: ResourceQuota objects that include PriorityClass as a scope were calculated incorrectly, leading to inaccurate quota usage tracking.
enrichment.affected: Users who define ResourceQuota with a PriorityClass scope (e.g., per‑priority‑class quota enforcement) were seeing incorrect quota usage figures.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the quota calculation logic to correctly account for pods' PriorityClass when evaluating ResourceQuota usage.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now rely on accurate enforcement of ResourceQuota limits that are scoped by PriorityClass, preventing unintended over‑consumption of resources.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: the volume is not detached after the pod and PVC objects are deleted
bugOrRegression.author: cvvz

enrichment.problem: When a Pod and its associated PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) were deleted, the underlying volume was not detached, leaving stale volume attachments on the node.
enrichment.affected: Users running Pods with PersistentVolumeClaims (especially with CSI drivers) who delete Pods and PVCs could encounter lingering volume attachments.
enrichment.fix: Implemented logic to ensure that volume detachment is triggered when both the Pod and its PVC are removed, cleaning up the attachment state promptly.
enrichment.impact: Prevents resource leaks and attachment errors, improves reliability for workloads that use PVC-backed volumes, and avoids manual intervention to clean up stuck volume attachments.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a memory leak in the Kubernetes API server that occurs during APIService processing.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver leaked memory while processing APIService objects, causing memory usage to grow over time.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run the kube-apiserver and use APIService resources (e.g., aggregated API servers).
enrichment.fix: The code that handled APIService processing was updated to correctly release allocated memory, eliminating the leak.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unbounded memory growth in the API server, reducing the risk of out‑of‑memory crashes or degraded performance for clusters that use aggregated API servers.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a regression in kubectl and client-go discovery when configured with a server URL other than the root of a server.
bugOrRegression.author: ardaguclu

enrichment.problem: kubectl and client-go discovery failed when the API server was accessed via a URL that was not the root path (e.g., behind a reverse proxy or custom base path).
enrichment.affected: Anyone using kubectl or client-go with a non-root server URL (e.g., clusters exposed via reverse proxies, multi-tenant setups).
enrichment.fix: The discovery code in kubectl and client-go was updated to correctly handle server URLs that include a non-root base path, restoring proper API resource discovery.
enrichment.impact: Users can once again run kubectl commands and use client-go against API servers behind proxies or with custom base URLs, avoiding failures in resource discovery and enabling smooth cluster interactions.

bugOrRegression.description: Number of errors reported to the metric `storage_operation_duration_seconds_count` for emptyDir decreased significantly because previously one error was reported for each projected volume created.
bugOrRegression.author: mpatlasov

enrichment.problem: The metric `storage_operation_duration_seconds_count` was incremented for every projected volume created for an emptyDir, causing an inflated error count for emptyDir operations.
enrichment.affected: Users monitoring storage operation metrics, especially those running pods with emptyDir volumes that also use projected volumes.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the metric reporting logic so that only a single error is counted per emptyDir operation instead of one per projected volume.
enrichment.impact: Provides more accurate storage operation metrics, reducing false error alarms and improving observability for workloads that use emptyDir volumes.

bugOrRegression.description: Recreate DaemonSet pods completed with Succeeded phase
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: When a DaemonSet pod is recreated (e.g., during a rollout restart), the pod incorrectly finishes with a Succeeded phase instead of Remaining Running, causing the pod to be terminated and the DaemonSet to lose its desired daemon on the node.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that use DaemonSets, especially those that perform pod recreation via rollout restart or similar update mechanisms.
enrichment.fix: The DaemonSet controller logic was updated to correctly set the pod’s phase to Running after recreation, ensuring the pod stays alive as part of the DaemonSet.
enrichment.impact: DaemonSet workloads now stay healthy after restarts, preventing unexpected downtime for node‑level services such as log collectors, monitoring agents, or network daemons.

bugOrRegression.description: Resolves a spurious "Unknown discovery response content-type" error in client-go discovery requests by tolerating extra content-type parameters in API responses
bugOrRegression.author: seans3

enrichment.problem: Client-go discovery requests sometimes failed with an "Unknown discovery response content-type" error because the API server response included extra content-type parameters that the client did not recognize.
enrichment.affected: Any component using client-go discovery, such as kubectl, controller-manager and custom controllers/operators.
enrichment.fix: The client-go library now tolerates additional content-type parameters in discovery responses, preventing the spurious error.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of tools and controllers that rely on client-go discovery (e.g., kubectl, controller-manager, custom controllers), eliminating unexpected failures when the API server includes extra content-type metadata.

bugOrRegression.description: Setting a mirror pod's phase to Succeeded or Failed can prevent the corresponding static pod from restarting due mutation of a Kubelet cache.
bugOrRegression.author: smarterclayton

enrichment.problem: When a mirror pod's status phase was set to Succeeded or Failed, the kubelet mutated its internal cache, which prevented the associated static pod from being restarted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using static (manifest) pods on nodes; kubelet could fail to restart those pods after they reported Succeeded or Failed.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet cache handling has been corrected so that changing a mirror pod's phase no longer blocks the restart of the corresponding static pod.
enrichment.impact: Static pods (e.g., self‑hosted control‑plane components) can now reliably restart after termination, preventing unexpected downtime of critical node services.

bugOrRegression.description:
[KCCM] service controller: change the cloud controller manager to make `providerID` a predicate when synchronizing nodes. This change allows load balancer integrations to ensure that  the `providerID` is set when configuring
  load balancers and targets.
bugOrRegression.author: alexanderConstantinescu

enrichment.problem: The cloud controller manager did not require `providerID` to be set when synchronizing nodes, so load balancer integrations could attempt to configure load balancers and targets without a valid `providerID`, leading to misconfigurations or failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use cloud provider load‑balancer integrations (e.g., GCE, AWS, Azure) and rely on the cloud controller manager to sync node information for Service LB provisioning.
enrichment.fix: Updated the service controller in the cloud controller manager to make `providerID` a predicate for node synchronization, ensuring the field is present before load balancer resources are created or updated.
enrichment.impact: Load balancer services (e.g., Service type LoadBalancer) now reliably receive the correct node `providerID`, preventing provisioning errors and improving stability of traffic distribution in cloud environments.

other.description: A v2-level info log will be added, which will output the details of the pod being preempted, including victim and preemptor
other.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: When a pod is preempted, the scheduler did not emit detailed logs, making it hard for operators to understand which pods were victims and which were preemptors.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and developers who need visibility into pod preemption decisions.
enrichment.fix: Added a v2-level info log entry that prints the full details of the preemption event, including both the victim pod and the preemptor pod.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging of scheduling preemption events, helping operators troubleshoot resource contention and policy issues more quickly.

securityFixes.title: Bypassing enforce mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityFixes.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using ephemeral containers. The policy ensures pods running with a service account may only reference secrets specified in the service account's secrets field. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if the ServiceAccount admission plugin and the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation are used together with ephemeral containers.

**Note**: This only impacts the cluster if the ServiceAccount admission plugin is used (most cluster should have this on by default as recommended in https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#serviceaccount), the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation is used by a service account (this annotation is not added by default), and Pods are using ephemeral containers.

feature.description: Kubernetes 1.26.x is now built with Go 1.19.10
feature.author: puerco

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes releases prior to this update were built with an older Go version, which could miss recent Go security patches and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from the source tree are rebuilt with Go 1.19.10, affecting any cluster that upgrades to a 1.26.x release.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes 1.26.x is now built using Go 1.19.10, upgrading the toolchain for all binaries.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) benefit from the latest Go security fixes and compiler improvements, reducing potential attack surface and ensuring continued compatibility with newer Go ecosystem features.

bugOrRegression.description: Add DisruptionTarget condition to the pod preempted by Kubelet to make room for a critical pod
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: When kubelet preempts a pod to free resources for a critical pod, there was no explicit condition on the evicted pod, making it difficult for users and testing to know why the pod was terminated.
enrichment.affected: Pods that are preempted by the kubelet when a critical pod needs resources, and the users/operators monitoring those pods.
enrichment.fix: Introduce a new DisruptionTarget condition that is set on pods preempted by the kubelet for critical pods, exposing the preemption reason via the pod status.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging of pod preemptions, allowing operators and automated tests to detect that a pod was evicted to make room for a critical workload. This reduces confusion and aids in troubleshooting resource pressure scenarios.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug at kube-apiserver start where APIService objects for custom resources could be deleted and recreated.
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: During kube-apiserver startup, a bug could cause APIService objects for custom resources to be unintentionally deleted and then recreated, leading to temporary loss of access to those aggregated APIs.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use aggregated API servers with custom resources (APIService objects) could experience brief API unavailability on kube-apiserver restart.
enrichment.fix: The kube-apiserver start-up logic was corrected to preserve existing APIService objects for custom resources, preventing their deletion and unnecessary recreation.
enrichment.impact: Ensures continuous availability of custom resource APIs during kube-apiserver restarts, eliminating brief service disruptions and reducing load from unnecessary object churn.

bugOrRegression.description: If `kubeadm reset` finds no etcd member ID for the peer it removes during the `remove-etcd-member` phase, it continues immediately to other phases, instead of retrying the phase for up to 3 minutes before continuing.
bugOrRegression.author: dlipovetsky

enrichment.problem: During `kubeadm reset`, if the tool cannot find an etcd member ID for a peer during the `remove-etcd-member` phase, it skips retrying and immediately proceeds to subsequent phases.
enrichment.affected: Users running `kubeadm reset` on clusters where an etcd member may already be absent or its ID cannot be retrieved.
enrichment.fix: The reset logic now retries the `remove-etcd-member` phase for up to 3 minutes when the member ID is missing before moving on, ensuring proper cleanup.
enrichment.impact: Prevents incomplete etcd cleanup during a cluster reset, avoiding orphaned etcd members and potential inconsistencies when re‑initializing or joining the cluster.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a bug where the static pod changes detection logic is inconsistent with kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: Kubeadm's logic for detecting changes to static pod manifests was not aligned with kubelet's detection, leading to cases where updates to static pods were not recognized or applied correctly.
enrichment.affected: Users who manage static pods via kubeadm (e.g., control‑plane static pods) could see pods not updating after manifest changes.
enrichment.fix: The detection algorithm in kubeadm was updated to match kubelet's behavior, ensuring consistent identification of static pod changes.
enrichment.impact: Clusters bootstrapped with kubeadm will now reliably pick up updates to static pods, preventing stale or out‑of‑date pods and reducing manual intervention or unexpected downtime.

apiChange.description: GCE does not support LoadBalancer Services with ports with different protocols (TCP and UDP)
apiChange.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: GCE cloud provider cannot provision a LoadBalancer Service that includes ports using different protocols (e.g., a mix of TCP and UDP). Such Services were previously accepted but would not function correctly.
enrichment.affected: GCE users creating LoadBalancer Services with both TCP and UDP ports; workloads relying on a single Service for mixed protocols.
enrichment.fix: Added validation in the GCE cloud provider logic to reject LoadBalancer Services that specify mixed protocols, ensuring users receive a clear error and must create separate Services for each protocol.
enrichment.impact: Prevents silent failures when exposing workloads with mixed‑protocol ports on GCE. Users must split the Service into separate TCP and UDP LoadBalancers, avoiding unexpected traffic loss.

feature.description: Kubernetes 1.26.x is now built with Go 1.20.5
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes 1.26.x was built with an older Go toolchain, which may miss recent language/runtime security fixes and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) built from source in the 1.26.x series.
enrichment.fix: The release series is now compiled using Go 1.20.5, updating the build toolchain for all Kubernetes binaries.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components gain the security patches, bug fixes, and performance enhancements shipped in Go 1.20.5, reducing the risk of Go‑level vulnerabilities and improving runtime efficiency without requiring any user‑side changes.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.6
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was previously built with an older Go version, which could miss security patches, performance improvements, and compatibility fixes provided by newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and users building from source, including kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, and related tooling.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.20.6 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries now benefit from the latest Go security updates, bug fixes, and language/runtime improvements, reducing the risk of hidden vulnerabilities and improving overall stability and performance for clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix component status calling etcd health endpoint over http which exposed kubernetes to the risk of complete watch starvation and is inconsistent with other etcd probing done by kube-apiserver.
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: The component status health check queried the etcd health endpoint over plain HTTP, creating a security exposure and causing the risk of complete watch starvation, and it was inconsistent with the TLS‑based probing used by the kube-apiserver.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where the kube‑apiserver's componentstatus endpoint performed health checks against etcd over HTTP could experience watch starvation and insecure communication.
enrichment.fix: Updated the component status logic to probe the etcd health endpoint using the same secure (HTTPS/TLS) configuration as the kube‑apiserver, aligning the health checks and preventing watch starvation.
enrichment.impact: Ensures reliable watch streams and control‑plane health checks, eliminates an insecure HTTP call to etcd, and brings component‑status probing in line with other apiserver checks, improving cluster stability and security.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix cronjob controller handling of complex schedules, like "30 6-16/4 * * 1-5", for example
bugOrRegression.author: kmala

enrichment.problem: The cronjob controller failed to correctly handle complex cron schedule expressions (e.g., '30 6-16/4 * * 1-5'), leading to missed or incorrect job executions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running CronJob objects with complex schedule expressions; workloads depending on precise periodic execution.
enrichment.fix: Updated the cronjob controller logic in kube-controller-manager to properly parse and evaluate complex schedule strings, ensuring jobs are created at the intended times.
enrichment.impact: Users with CronJob resources that use advanced cron syntax will now have reliable execution of scheduled jobs, preventing missed runs and potential service disruptions.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a performance issue where pods weren't created/deleted in parallel for a StatefulSet with podManagementPolicy: Parallel.
bugOrRegression.author: aleksandra-malinowska

enrichment.problem: When a StatefulSet used podManagementPolicy: Parallel, the controller created and deleted pods sequentially instead of in parallel, slowing down scaling operations.
enrichment.affected: Users running StatefulSets with podManagementPolicy: Parallel experienced slower scaling because pod creation/deletion was serialized.
enrichment.fix: The StatefulSet controller (in kube‑controller‑manager) was updated to create and delete Pods concurrently when the parallel policy is set.
enrichment.impact: StatefulSets that rely on parallel pod management now scale up and down faster, reducing rollout time and improving overall performance for workloads that use this feature.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed file permission issues that happened during update of Secret/ConfigMap/projected volume when fsGroup is used. The problem caused a race condition where application gets intermittent permission denied error when reading files that were just updated, before the correct permissions were applied.
bugOrRegression.author: furkatgofurov7

enrichment.problem: When a Secret, ConfigMap, or projected volume is updated while a pod uses fsGroup, the kubelet applied new file contents before updating the file permissions, creating a race condition that caused intermittent "permission denied" errors for applications reading the freshly updated files.
enrichment.affected: Pods using Secret, ConfigMap, or projected volumes with fsGroup set (e.g., workloads that need group‑based file permissions).
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the volume update logic to set the correct fsGroup permissions on the files before they become visible to the pod, eliminating the race condition during Secret/ConfigMap/projected volume updates.
enrichment.impact: Pods that mount Secrets, ConfigMaps, or projected volumes with an fsGroup will no longer experience intermittent permission denied errors after volume updates, improving reliability of applications that rely on these volume types.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed vSphere cloud provider not to skip detach volumes from nodes at kube-controller-startup.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: The vSphere cloud provider incorrectly skipped detaching volumes from nodes during kube-controller-manager startup, leaving stale volume attachments after a controller restart.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running on vSphere that use the vSphere cloud provider for volume management, especially when the kube-controller-manager restarts.
enrichment.fix: Updated the vSphere cloud provider logic to ensure volume detach operations are executed during controller startup, preventing the skip.
enrichment.impact: Prevents stale volume attachments that could cause attach errors or pod scheduling failures, improving reliability for clusters running on vSphere with persistent storage.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: explicitly set `priority` for static pods with `priorityClassName: system-node-critical`
bugOrRegression.author: champtar

enrichment.problem: Static pods created by kubeadm that specified `priorityClassName: system-node-critical` did not have the `priority` field set, so they could be treated as lower‑priority pods and be preempted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use kubeadm to bootstrap control‑plane static pods with `priorityClassName: system-node-critical`.
enrichment.fix: Kubeadm now copies the priority derived from the `system-node-critical` PriorityClass into the static pod manifest by explicitly setting the `priority` field.
enrichment.impact: Critical control‑plane static pods (e.g., kube-apiserver, controller‑manager, scheduler) are now scheduled with the correct high priority, preventing unintended preemption and improving cluster stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Only declare Job as finished after removing all Pod finalizers to avoid orphan Pods
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: Jobs were marked as completed before their Pods' finalizers were removed, which could leave orphan Pods that never get cleaned up.
enrichment.affected: Users running batch Jobs where Pods have finalizers; orphan Pods could persist after Job completion.
enrichment.fix: The Job controller now waits until all Pod finalizers are removed before declaring the Job finished, ensuring Pods are fully terminated.
enrichment.impact: Prevents resource leaks and dangling Pods after a Job completes, improving reliability of batch workloads and cluster resource management.

bugOrRegression.description: The Daemonset controller creates replacements for terminal Pods, which can appear during VM preemptions or when using Pod finalizers
bugOrRegression.author: alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: The DaemonSet controller incorrectly created replacement Pods for Pods that were already terminating (terminal Pods). This could happen during VM preemptions or when Pods used finalizers, leading to unnecessary Pod churn and potential resource waste.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running DaemonSets, particularly in cloud environments with VM preemptions or applications that rely on Pod finalizers.
enrichment.fix: The DaemonSet controller now skips creating replacement Pods for Pods that are in a terminal state, preventing redundant Pod creation during VM preemptions or when Pod finalizers are in use.
enrichment.impact: Reduces unnecessary Pod creation and resource consumption for DaemonSet workloads, especially in environments with frequent VM preemptions or where Pods use finalizers. Improves cluster stability and resource efficiency.

bugOrRegression.description: This PR adds additional validation for endpoint ip configuration while iterating through queried endpoint list.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: Endpoints could be created or updated with invalid IP configuration because the code lacked sufficient validation when processing the list of queried endpoints.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Services/Endpoints, particularly on Windows nodes, could experience connectivity issues due to invalid endpoint IPs.
enrichment.fix: Added extra validation checks for endpoint IP configuration during iteration of the endpoint list, ensuring only valid IPs are accepted.
enrichment.impact: Prevents malformed endpoint IPs that could lead to network connectivity failures or service disruption, especially in Windows clusters where networking handling differs.

bugOrRegression.description: Updated cAdvisor to v0.46.1 - Fix metrics in cri-o when a container restarts
bugOrRegression.author: harche

enrichment.problem: When using the CRI-O container runtime, cAdvisor failed to update container metrics after a container restart, resulting in stale or missing metric values.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run CRI‑O as the container runtime and rely on kubelet‑exposed metrics for observability and automation.
enrichment.fix: cAdvisor was upgraded to v0.46.1, which includes a fix that correctly refreshes metrics for containers managed by CRI‑O when they restart.
enrichment.impact: Provides accurate per‑container metrics for monitoring tools (e.g., Prometheus) and prevents misleading alerts or scaling decisions that could arise from incorrect metric data.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization on Windows nodes leads to privilege escalation
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization on Windows nodes leads to privilege escalation
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

apiChange.description: Aggregated discovery now returns `responseKind: {}` for resources which are missing group/version/kind information, to ensure compatibility with v0.26.0-v0.26.3 clients.
apiChange.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Aggregated discovery responses omitted group, version, and kind fields for some resources, causing incompatibility and errors in clients from v0.26.0 to v0.26.3.
enrichment.affected: Clients using Kubernetes v0.26.0‑v0.26.3 that perform aggregated discovery could not handle missing group/version/kind information.
enrichment.fix: The server now always includes a `responseKind:{}` object for resources missing those fields, ensuring older clients can parse the response without failure.
enrichment.impact: Restores compatibility for users running v0.26.x clients, preventing discovery‑related crashes or mis‑behaviour when interacting with newer API servers.

feature.description:
Kubeadm: generate CA certificates with a start time that is offset 5 minutes in the past relative to the current system time to workaround cases of clock desync.
  client-go: allow to set NotBefore in NewSelfSignedCACert()
feature.author: champtar

enrichment.problem: When the system clock is behind, kubeadm‑generated CA certificates have a NotBefore timestamp that is later than the actual time, causing the certificates to be considered not yet valid and breaking cluster bootstrapping and API communication.
enrichment.affected: Users bootstrapping clusters with kubeadm on nodes whose system clocks are out of sync; developers using client-go to generate self‑signed CA certificates.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now generates CA certificates with a NotBefore time offset 5 minutes into the past. client-go adds a NewSelfSignedCACert option to explicitly set NotBefore, supporting the same workaround.
enrichment.impact: Clusters initialized with kubeadm on nodes with clock skew can start successfully, and any component using client‑go to create self‑signed CAs can avoid validity‑time issues. This improves reliability of cluster creation and upgrades in environments where perfect time sync cannot be guaranteed.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.7
feature.author: jeremyrickard

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were being built with an older Go version, which may lack recent security fixes and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, CI pipelines, and downstream distributions that compile the binaries.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.20.7, bringing the codebase up to a newer, supported compiler version.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that future Kubernetes releases benefit from Go security patches, performance improvements, and language features, reducing potential supply‑chain risk for users and distributors.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix Topology Aware Hints not working when the `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` label is added after Node creation

enrichment.problem: Pods that relied on Topology Aware Hints were not receiving correct placement hints when the `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` label was added to a Node after the Node had already been created, causing suboptimal or failed scheduling decisions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where node zone labels are added after node creation; any Pods that use Topology Aware Hints for placement.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now watches for updates to the `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` label on existing Nodes and recomputes Topology Aware Hints accordingly, ensuring hints are accurate regardless of when the zone label is applied.
enrichment.impact: Improves pod placement accuracy for workloads that use Topology Aware Hints, preventing uneven distribution across zones and reducing scheduling failures in environments where node zone labels are applied post‑creation.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a data race in TopologyCache when `AddHints` and `SetNodes` are called concurrently
bugOrRegression.author: tnqn

enrichment.problem: A data race existed in the scheduler's TopologyCache when the AddHints and SetNodes methods were invoked concurrently, which could lead to corrupted cache state, incorrect topology hints, and potential scheduler crashes or mis‑placements.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable topology‑aware scheduling features such as topology spread constraints, NUMA node hints, or any workload relying on the scheduler's TopologyCache.
enrichment.fix: Synchronize access to TopologyCache by adding proper locking around AddHints and SetNodes, eliminating the race condition and ensuring cache consistency.
enrichment.impact: Stabilizes the scheduler for clusters that use topology‑aware scheduling (e.g., NUMA or node resource topology hints), preventing crashes and ensuring pods are placed according to correct topology information.

bugOrRegression.description: Revert kubelet prober metrics `pod` tag to include actual pod name
bugOrRegression.author: a7i

enrichment.problem: Kubelet probe metrics were missing the actual pod name in the `pod` label, making it difficult to associate metric data with specific pods.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that rely on kubelet probe metrics for monitoring or alerting, especially those that filter or group by pod name.
enrichment.fix: Reverted the recent change so that the `pod` tag on kubelet prober metrics now includes the real pod name again.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging by allowing monitoring systems to correctly attribute probe metrics to the originating pods.

bugOrRegression.description:
Update kube-apiserver's priority & fairness work estimator such that 'max seats' is MIN(0.15 x nominalCL, nominalCL / handSize)
  This fixes a bug where clients with requests using hand size x max seats greater than the nominal concurrency limit can starve other requests in the same priority level.
bugOrRegression.author: andrewsykim

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver's priority and fairness estimator could assign a 'max seats' value that, when multiplied by the hand size, exceeded the nominal concurrency limit, causing requests from one client to starve other requests at the same priority level.
enrichment.affected: Clients using the kube-apiserver priority and fairness feature could experience request starvation, affecting workload APIs that share the same priority level.
enrichment.fix: The estimator now caps 'max seats' to the minimum of 0.15 × nominalCL and nominalCL / handSize, preventing the hand size × max seats product from surpassing the nominal concurrency limit and eliminating starvation.
enrichment.impact: API request handling becomes fairer and more predictable, ensuring that no single client can monopolize the apiserver's concurrency capacity. This improves overall cluster responsiveness and stability for workloads relying on priority and fairness.

bugOrRegression.description: Update the Event series starting count when emitting isomorphic events from 1 to 2.
bugOrRegression.author: dgrisonnet

enrichment.problem: When emitting isomorphic events, the series count started at 1, leading to off‑by‑one counts and confusing event series numbers for users monitoring or debugging workloads.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that rely on Kubernetes event series counts (e.g., monitoring dashboards, kubectl event listings).
enrichment.fix: The event handling logic now initializes the series starting count at 2 for isomorphic events, ensuring correct sequential numbering.
enrichment.impact: Provides accurate event series numbers, improving observability and reducing confusion when correlating related events.

apiChange.description:
Fixed a bug where CEL expressions in CRD validation rules would incorrectly compute a high estimated cost for functions that return strings, lists or maps.
  The incorrect cost was evident when the result of a function was used in subsequent operations.
apiChange.author: jpbetz

enrichment.problem: CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) validation rules using CEL expressions incorrectly calculated a high estimated cost for functions that return strings, lists, or maps, causing validation to be erroneously rejected when those function results were used in subsequent operations.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enforce CRDs with CEL validation rules calling functions that return strings, lists, or maps; developers writing such CRDs.
enrichment.fix: The CEL cost estimation logic was updated to correctly compute costs for functions returning string, list, and map types, ensuring the estimated cost matches the actual evaluation cost.
enrichment.impact: CRD validation now works as intended for objects that use CEL functions returning complex types, preventing false validation failures and eliminating the need for work‑arounds in CRD definitions.

apiChange.description: Mark Job onPodConditions as optional in pod failure policy
apiChange.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The `onPodConditions` field in a Job's pod failure policy was mandatory, causing validation failures for users who wanted to define a pod failure policy without specifying any pod condition triggers.
enrichment.affected: Users defining Job resources with pod failure policies that did not need pod condition triggers were blocked by strict validation.
enrichment.fix: The `onPodConditions` field is now marked as optional in the Job API schema, allowing jobs to omit it while still using other pod failure policy settings.
enrichment.impact: Users can create Jobs with pod failure policies more flexibly, avoiding unnecessary validation errors and simplifying Job specifications.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.8
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss critical language fixes and security patches.
enrichment.affected: Developers, CI pipelines, and downstream distributors that build Kubernetes from source.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile the codebase with Go 1.20.8.
enrichment.impact: Improves build reliability, incorporates upstream Go security fixes, and aligns the cluster components with the supported Go version for future development.

bugOrRegression.description: Cherry-pick #115769: Fix the problem Pod terminating stuck because of trying to umount not actual mounted dir.
bugOrRegression.author: cartermckinnon

enrichment.problem: Pods could remain in the Terminating state because the kubelet attempted to unmount a directory that was never actually mounted, causing the termination process to hang.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that reaches Terminating while having volume mounts that were not correctly recorded as mounted on the node. The issue manifested on nodes running the kubelet.
enrichment.fix: Added a guard in the kubelet unmount logic to verify that the target path is really mounted before attempting unmount, preventing the stale unmount call and allowing pods to finish termination normally.
enrichment.impact: Pods can now terminate cleanly without getting stuck, freeing resources and avoiding potential node resource exhaustion. This improves reliability for workloads that use volume mounts.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a concurrent map access in TopologyCache's `HasPopulatedHints` method.
bugOrRegression.author: Miciah

enrichment.problem: A race condition caused concurrent map reads/writes in the TopologyCache.HasPopulatedHints method, which could lead to a panic in the scheduler.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable topology‑aware scheduling or rely on topology hints for pod placement could experience scheduler panics under load.
enrichment.fix: Added proper synchronization to protect the map access, eliminating the concurrent access bug.
enrichment.impact: Prevents scheduler crashes when topology hints are evaluated, ensuring reliable pod placement and overall cluster stability for clusters using topology‑aware scheduling.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a 1.26 regression scheduling bug by ensuring that preemption is skipped when a PreFilter plugin returns `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.26 a regression caused the scheduler to perform preemption even when a PreFilter plugin returned `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`, leading to unnecessary or incorrect preemption attempts and scheduling failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes 1.26 that use PreFilter plugins returning `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`; pods scheduled by the kube-scheduler could be incorrectly preempted.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now checks the result of PreFilter plugins and skips the preemption phase when the status is `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`.
enrichment.impact: Prevents spurious preemption cycles, restores expected scheduling behavior, and improves cluster stability for workloads that rely on custom PreFilter plugins.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug where images pinned by the container runtime can be garbage collected by kubelet.
bugOrRegression.author: ruiwen-zhao

enrichment.problem: Kubelet could incorrectly garbage collect container images that were explicitly pinned by the container runtime, causing those images to disappear even though they were marked as required.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet with a container runtime that pins images; any pods that depend on those pinned images.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now respects the image‑pinning flag from the container runtime and excludes such images from its garbage‑collection process.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that pinned images remain available on the node, preventing pod start failures or restarts caused by missing images and improving node stability for workloads that rely on image pinning.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes issue https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cloud-provider-azure/issues/4230 and removes the additional filtering on `NotReady` nodes by the azure cloud provider code
bugOrRegression.author: alexanderConstantinescu

enrichment.problem: The Azure cloud provider incorrectly applied extra filtering that excluded nodes in the NotReady state from cloud‑provider operations, causing pods to be considered unschedulable or load balancer updates to ignore those nodes.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters on Azure that rely on the Azure cloud provider, especially workloads that experience node health fluctuations.
enrichment.fix: The extra NotReady node filtering logic has been removed from the Azure cloud provider code, allowing NotReady nodes to be processed according to the standard Kubernetes behavior.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using the Azure cloud provider will no longer experience unnecessary scheduling failures or load‑balancer inconsistencies when nodes temporarily enter NotReady, improving reliability during node health transitions.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes regression in 1.26.5 causing running pods with devices to be terminated if kubelet is restarted
bugOrRegression.author: ffromani

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.26.5 caused pods that use device plugins to be terminated whenever the kubelet was restarted.
enrichment.affected: Users running pods that request devices via the device plugin framework; any workload that experiences a kubelet restart would see those pods terminated.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic was corrected/restored so that pods with allocated devices are preserved across kubelet restarts, preventing unexpected termination.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on hardware devices (e.g., GPUs, SR-IOV, other device plugins) remain running after a kubelet restart, avoiding service disruption and data loss for workloads that depend on those devices.

bugOrRegression.description: Ignore context canceled from validate and mutate webhook
bugOrRegression.author: divyasri537

enrichment.problem: When an admission webhook (validate or mutate) returned a context.Canceled error, the API server treated it as a failure, causing API requests to be rejected unnecessarily.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or updating resources that trigger admission webhooks experienced unexpected rejections.
enrichment.fix: The API server now ignores context.Canceled errors from admission webhooks, treating them as a no‑op instead of a failure.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of create/modify operations that involve admission webhooks, preventing spurious request failures when a webhook is cancelled or unavailable.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix nil pointer when etcd member is already removed
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm panics with a nil pointer dereference when attempting to remove an etcd member that has already been removed, causing the command to fail.
enrichment.affected: Clusters managed with kubeadm where an etcd member removal is attempted after the member has already been removed; this primarily impacts cluster operators.
enrichment.fix: Added defensive checks in kubeadm's etcd member removal logic to handle already‑removed members gracefully, preventing the nil pointer panic.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can now safely run `kubeadm reset` or etcd member removal operations without the tool crashing, ensuring cluster lifecycle commands continue to work and reducing downtime for cluster maintenance.

other.description: When retrieving event resources, the reportingController and reportingInstance fields in the event will contain values.
other.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: Events returned by the API were missing the `reportingController` and `reportingInstance` fields, leaving users without information about which controller generated the event.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that read Event resources (e.g., kubectl, monitoring systems, custom controllers) were unable to see the reporting controller/instance information.
enrichment.fix: The API server now populates the `reportingController` and `reportingInstance` fields when events are retrieved, ensuring these values are always present in the event object.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging by allowing users and tools to identify the source controller of events, enabling more accurate monitoring and troubleshooting.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version, lacking recent security patches, performance improvements, and platform compatibility updates.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy) and any clusters running the released binaries.
enrichment.fix: Upgrade the build toolchain to Go 1.20.10 and rebuild all Kubernetes components with this version.
enrichment.impact: All users receive Kubernetes binaries that incorporate the latest Go security fixes, performance enhancements, and compatibility updates, reducing potential vulnerabilities and improving overall stability.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with older Go versions, which may lack recent language improvements, security patches, and performance optimizations.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from source (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.)
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now built using Go 1.20.9, incorporating the latest compiler and runtime enhancements.
enrichment.impact: Provides security and performance benefits to every Kubernetes component and ensures compatibility with future Go releases, reducing maintenance overhead for developers and downstream distributors.

bugOrRegression.description: Adds an opt-in mitigation for http/2 DOS vulnerabilities for CVE-2023-44487 and CVE-2023-39325 for the API server when the client is unauthenticated. The mitigation may be enabled by setting the `UnauthenticatedHTTP2DOSMitigation` feature gate to `true` (it is disabled by default). An API server fronted by an L7 load balancer that already mitigates these http/2 attacks may choose not to enable the kube-apiserver mitigation to avoid disrupting load balancer → kube-apiserver connections if http/2 requests from multiple clients share the same backend connection. An API server on a private network may choose not to enable the kube-apiserver mitigation to prevent performance regressions for unauthenticated clients. Authenticated requests rely on the fix in golang.org/x/net v0.17.0 alone. https://issue.k8s.io/121197 tracks further mitigation of http/2 attacks by authenticated clients.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: Unauthenticated clients can exploit HTTP/2 protocol vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-44487, CVE-2023-39325) to cause denial‑of‑service on the kube‑apiserver, as no mitigation was present by default.
enrichment.affected: Unauthenticated clients communicating with the kube‑apiserver, especially those behind L7 load balancers or on private networks.
enrichment.fix: Introduces an optional mitigation controlled by the UnauthenticatedHTTP2DOSMitigation feature gate. When enabled, the apiserver throttles or rejects malicious HTTP/2 patterns from unauthenticated requests. Authenticated clients already benefit from upstream Go net library fixes.
enrichment.impact: Provides protection against known HTTP/2 DoS attacks for clusters exposed to unauthenticated traffic, while allowing operators to disable it if a front‑end load balancer already handles the mitigation or to avoid potential performance impact.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug in cronjob controller where already created jobs may be missing from the status.
bugOrRegression.author: andrewsykim

enrichment.problem: The cronjob controller could omit already created Job objects from the CronJob's status, causing the reported active/completed job counts to be inaccurate.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster running CronJob resources could see stale or incomplete status information, especially those that monitor or react to CronJob status fields.
enrichment.fix: The controller logic was updated to ensure that any Job that already exists is included when building the CronJob status, so the status now reflects all relevant Jobs.
enrichment.impact: Users and automation that rely on CronJob status (e.g., monitoring, scaling decisions, UI dashboards) will see accurate job counts, preventing confusion and potential misbehaviour caused by missing status entries.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a 1.26.7 regression where kube-controller-manager can crash when StatefulSet with Parallel policy and PVC labels is scaled up.
bugOrRegression.author: aleksandra-malinowska

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager crashes during scaling of a StatefulSet that uses the Parallel podManagementPolicy and has PersistentVolumeClaim labels, a regression introduced in v1.26.7.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running StatefulSets with podManagementPolicy=Parallel and PVCs that have labels; scaling operations could cause the controller manager to crash.
enrichment.fix: The controller manager code handling StatefulSet scaling with PVC label Selector was corrected, preventing the panic and ensuring the manager remains stable when such StatefulSets are scaled up.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliability of the control plane for workloads that use Parallel‑policy StatefulSets with PVC labels, avoiding controller‑manager downtime and ensuring StatefulSet scaling functions correctly.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed attaching volumes after detach errors. Now volumes that failed to detach are not treated as attached, Kubernetes will make sure they are fully attached before they can be used by pods.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: When a volume detach operation fails, the volume is still marked as attached, allowing pods to try to use it before it is fully attached again, leading to pod failures or possible data corruption.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use persistent volumes (e.g., StatefulSets, Deployments) could experience failures or data issues when a previous detach error occurred.
enrichment.fix: Updated the attach/detach logic so that volumes that failed to detach are no longer considered attached. The system now ensures a volume is fully attached before it can be used by a pod.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of storage operations, preventing pods from crashing or accessing incomplete volume states, reducing risk of data loss for workloads that rely on persistent volumes.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug where Services using finalizers may hold onto ClusterIP and/or NodePort allocated resources for longer than expected if the finalizer is removed using the status subresource
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: Services that have finalizers can retain their allocated ClusterIP and/or NodePort after the finalizer is removed via the status subresource, causing the resources to remain allocated longer than intended.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster where Services use finalizers and are deleted or modified via the status subresource. Cluster administrators and workloads that create/delete Services are impacted.
enrichment.fix: The bug is fixed so that when a Service's finalizer is cleared through the status subresource, the Service controller promptly releases any associated ClusterIP and NodePort resources.
enrichment.impact: Prevents leaking of ClusterIP and NodePort resources, avoiding potential IP/port exhaustion and ensuring new Services can be created without hitting allocation limits. Improves cluster stability for workloads that rely on dynamic Service creation and deletion.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes creationTimestamp: null causing unnecessary writes to etcd
bugOrRegression.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: Objects with a nil creationTimestamp were being written to etcd on each update, causing unnecessary write operations.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or tool that creates or updates API objects where the creationTimestamp could be omitted or nil, including custom resources and test suites.
enrichment.fix: The API server now treats a null creationTimestamp as unchanged and skips redundant etcd writes, ensuring only legitimate updates are persisted.
enrichment.impact: Reduces needless etcd traffic and CPU usage, improving overall cluster performance and decreasing load on the datastore, especially in large clusters or heavy‑test environments.

bugOrRegression.description:
Revised the logic for DaemonSet rolling update to exclude nodes if scheduling constraints are not met.
  This eliminates the problem of rolling updates to a DaemonSet getting stuck around tolerations.
bugOrRegression.author: mochizuki875

enrichment.problem: DaemonSet rolling updates could become stuck when some nodes do not satisfy the DaemonSet's scheduling constraints such as tolerations, preventing the update from completing.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running DaemonSets that use tolerations or other scheduling constraints; administrators performing rolling updates of such DaemonSets.
enrichment.fix: The rolling update logic was revised to skip nodes whose constraints are not met, allowing the DaemonSet update to progress without being blocked by unschedulable nodes.
enrichment.impact: Updates to DaemonSets now complete reliably, reducing manual intervention and downtime for workloads that rely on DaemonSets with tolerations or other placement constraints.

bugOrRegression.description: Sometimes, the scheduler incorrectly placed a pod in the "unschedulable" queue instead of the "backoff" queue. This happened when some plugin previously declared the pod as "unschedulable" and then in a later attempt encounters some other error. Scheduling of that pod then got delayed by up to five minutes, after which periodic flushing moved the pod back into the "active" queue.
bugOrRegression.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler sometimes moved a pod to the "unschedulable" queue instead of the "backoff" queue when a plugin first marked the pod unschedulable and a later scheduling attempt encountered a different error. This caused the pod to be delayed for up to five minutes before being flushed back to the active queue.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that is scheduled by the kube-scheduler and encounters a plugin‑reported unschedulable status followed by a later error could be delayed. The issue affects workloads that rely on scheduler plugins and experience transient scheduling errors.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler queue handling logic was corrected so that once a pod has entered the backoff flow, subsequent errors keep it in the backoff queue rather than incorrectly re‑queuing it as unschedulable. This prevents the unnecessary five‑minute delay.
enrichment.impact: Pods are scheduled more promptly, eliminating an artificial delay and improving overall cluster scheduling latency for workloads that encounter transient errors after an initial unschedulable status.

other.description: Etcd: update to v3.5.9
other.author: nikhita

enrichment.problem: The Kubernetes distribution bundled an older etcd version that contained known bugs and security vulnerabilities, risking cluster stability and data integrity.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster that runs the built‑in etcd server (typical single‑node or stacked control‑plane setups) could be impacted by the previous bugs or vulnerabilities.
enrichment.fix: Bumps the bundled etcd binary to v3.5.9, which includes upstream security patches, bug fixes, and stability improvements.
enrichment.impact: Clusters get the latest etcd fixes without manual upgrades, reducing the risk of data loss, security exploits, and operational issues for all workloads using the control‑plane datastore.

other.description: Fixes an issue where the vsphere cloud provider will not trust a certificate if:

enrichment.problem: The vSphere cloud provider failed to trust a TLS certificate under certain conditions, causing connections to the vSphere API to be rejected.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using the vSphere cloud provider, particularly those that rely on custom or self‑signed TLS certificates for vSphere API access.
enrichment.fix: The certificate verification logic in the vSphere cloud provider was corrected to properly trust the relevant certificates, ensuring successful TLS handshakes.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use the vSphere cloud provider with custom or self‑signed certificates can now connect to vSphere services without errors, restoring expected functionality and avoiding disruption.

other.description: The issuer of the certificate is unknown (x509.UnknownAuthorityError)

enrichment.problem: Components failed TLS connections because the certificate’s issuer could not be verified, resulting in x509.UnknownAuthorityError.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that provision custom TLS certificates for the API server or other components (e.g., kubelet, controller‑manager) were unable to communicate, leading to degraded control‑plane functionality.
enrichment.fix: The change updates the certificate verification logic to correctly recognise and trust the configured Certificate Authority, allowing TLS handshakes to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Restores secure communication between Kubernetes control‑plane components and workloads that use custom or non‑default CAs, preventing outages caused by failed API calls.

other.description: The requested name does not match the set of authorized names (x509.HostnameError)

enrichment.problem: TLS connections to the API server failed when the server's certificate did not contain the requested hostname, resulting in a generic error instead of a clear x509.HostnameError message.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes component that establishes a TLS connection to the API server with a hostname not covered by the server's certificate, e.g., kubectl and kubelet.
enrichment.fix: The validation logic now correctly checks the requested host against the set of authorized names in the server's X.509 certificate and returns a detailed x509.HostnameError when there is a mismatch.
enrichment.impact: Clients such as kubectl, kubelet, and other components get a precise error, making troubleshooting of misconfigured certificates easier and preventing silent connection failures.

other.description: The error surfaced after attempting a connection contains one of the substrings: "certificate is not trusted" or "certificate signed by unknown authority"
other.author: MadhavJivrajani

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes cloud provider integrations failed to establish connections when the remote endpoint presented a TLS certificate that was not trusted or signed by an unknown authority, resulting in connection errors containing the substrings "certificate is not trusted" or "certificate signed by unknown authority".
enrichment.affected: Clusters running cloud provider components (cloud‑controller‑manager or controller‑manager) with TLS certificates that are self‑signed or signed by a non‑standard CA.
enrichment.fix: The cloud provider connection logic was updated to correctly handle custom or untrusted TLS certificates by allowing the specification of additional trusted CAs (or by adjusting verification behavior), preventing the premature failure of cloud-controller-manager operations.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using cloud provider integrations that rely on TLS connections to external services (e.g., custom cloud controllers, load balancers, storage APIs) can now communicate successfully, restoring normal provisioning, scaling, and health‑checking functionality.

other.description: Set the resolution for the job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric from 4ms to 1min
other.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric was recorded with a 4 ms resolution, creating high cardinality and excessive load on metric collection systems.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that collect kube‑controller‑manager job controller metrics, especially users with Prometheus or other monitoring setups that scrape these metrics.
enrichment.fix: The metric's resolution was changed to 1 minute, dramatically coarsening the recorded values and reducing the number of time‑series generated.
enrichment.impact: Reduces memory and CPU usage in the kube‑controller‑manager and downstream monitoring systems, leading to more efficient scraping and lower risk of metric over‑collection impacting cluster performance.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization in in-tree storage plugin leads to privilege escalation on Windows nodes
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods and persistent volumes on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they are using an in-tree storage plugin for Windows nodes.

apiChange.description: Retry NodeStageVolume calls if CSI node driver is not running
apiChange.author: rohitssingh

enrichment.problem: When the CSI node driver is not running, kubelet's NodeStageVolume call fails and is not retried, causing volume staging to fail and pods that depend on the volume cannot start.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use CSI volumes and the nodes where the CSI driver is not running; cluster administrators who experience pod start delays due to driver downtime.
enrichment.fix: Implemented retry logic in kubelet for NodeStageVolume calls when the CSI node driver is not running, allowing the operation to be re-attempted once the driver becomes available.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of CSI volume provisioning, reduces pod start failures, and eliminates the need for manual intervention to restart pods or drivers when the node driver is temporarily unavailable.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go release, missing the security, performance, and compatibility improvements introduced in newer Go versions.
enrichment.affected: Any user or distribution that builds Kubernetes from source—effectively all components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, etc.)—are impacted by the updated build toolchain.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile the entire Kubernetes codebase with Go 1.20.11.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components built from source now benefit from Go 1.20.11 bug fixes and security patches, improving reliability and future compatibility without changing runtime behavior.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix 121094 by re-introducing the readiness predicate for externalTrafficPolicy: Local services.
bugOrRegression.author: alexanderConstantinescu

enrichment.problem: Services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local were missing the readiness predicate, causing nodes without ready pods to be marked as ready endpoints and receive traffic, leading to request failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local, especially those behind cloud provider load balancers, could see dropped or misrouted traffic.
enrichment.fix: Re‑introduced the readiness predicate in the service controller so that only nodes with ready pods are considered when computing endpoints for externalTrafficPolicy=Local services.
enrichment.impact: Ensures traffic from external load balancers is only sent to nodes that have ready pods, preventing connection errors and improving reliability for workloads that rely on local traffic routing.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixed a regression in default 1.26 configurations, which enabled PodDisruptionConditions by default, 
  that prevented the control plane's pod garbage collector from deleting pods that contained duplicated field keys (env. variables with repeated keys or container ports).
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: A regression in the default 1.26 configuration enabled the PodDisruptionConditions feature by default, causing the control‑plane pod garbage collector to fail to delete pods that contain duplicated field keys such as repeated environment variable names or duplicate container ports.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes 1.26 with default configuration, and any workloads that create pods containing duplicate environment variable keys or duplicate container ports.
